data.title: Libreville grapples with water shortage
data.description: Gabon’s capital, Libreville, has been facing severe water shortages for several months, driven by low rainfall, ageing infrastructure and rising demand from a growing population. data.title: Spain's annual flamingo ringing begins
data.description: Hundreds of volunteers gathered at Spain’s Fuente de Piedra lake on Saturday for the annual flamingo-ringing initiative. Since the lake became a nature reserve in 1984, more than 200,000 flamingo chicks have hatched there. Each year, environmental authorities and volunteers tag the birds to track their movements across nature reserves in Europe and North Africa. This year, 600 chicks were ringed.

data.title: Movie paradise? How Malta became a magnet for big film shoots
data.description: EU’s smallest country has played ancient Rome, the Land of Spells and Bay of Pentos and draws more than 30 productions annually What links the Caribbean, ancient Rome, Enid Blyton’s Land of Spells, the south of France and the Bay of Pentos from Game of Thrones? They are all places that have been portrayed in recent and forthcoming films by a sunny archipelago in the Mediterranean Sea, no bigger in size than Sheffield. Malta has over the last decade risen to become one of the most popular places in Europe for American and British film-makers to set their works in, taking a lead in what has been described as an “arms race” to lure big movie productions with tax incentives. data.title: ‘I’ve sat at the very precipice of life’: Clarke Carlisle on gambling, depression – and survival
data.description: The former professional footballer has struggled with his mental health for most of his life. But it took five suicide attempts for him to admit how badly he wanted to end it. He talks about how he turned the corner – and his hopes for his new post with the charity Mind ‘How are you?” I ask Clarke Carlisle. Usually when you meet people it’s a nicety. Not with Carlisle. He smiles ecstatically. “I’m incredibly well, thank you. Yeah, really, really good,” says the former footballer and incoming chair of the mental health charity Mind. “I have been consistently well – not just stable, but well – for three or four years now.” Few people understand what it is to be mentally unwell quite like Carlisle does. And few understand what recovery means like he does. “It doesn’t happen by accident. Once you get stable that’s not the end of the journey. And that seems to be the MO of our society these days. You do something, you go into hospital and they patch you up, then send you on your way. And that’s the same with mental health. You might get some pills, have a counselling session, you might have a hug and a chat with someone, and they think that’s the end of the journey. And it’s not.” Continue reading...

data.title: ‘This is asking a lot of the buttocks’: my 23-hour Wagner marathon on a rock hard seat in a heatwave
data.description: How does it feel to be locked into a venue notorious for its unpadded seating to experience a full-throttle Ring cycle and more? Our critic found out at the 150th anniversary of the mighty Bayreuth festival Liszt and Bruckner were there from the start. Debussy, Mahler and Puccini all subsequently made the journey. So did writers from Virginia Woolf and Thomas Mann to WEB Du Bois, not to mention choreographer Sergei Diaghilev, anarchist Emma Goldman , British fascist Diana Mosley (wife of Oswald) and – most notoriously and fanatically – Adolf Hitler. Culturally and politically, Germany’s Bayreuth festival doesn’t so much have baggage as its own industrial-scale luggage hangar. But it’s also prized as the ultimate place to hear Richard Wagner ’s operas. One hundred and fifty years after the composer launched the festival with the premiere of his epic Ring cycle, tickets for this summer’s edition sold out within 90 minutes. No mean feat for a theatre with famously uncomfortable seats, no air conditioning and only one man’s music on the menu. The shortest work lasts two-and-a-half hours without a break. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Even the good guys were doing bad things’: the wild, twisted story behind the new Tiger King
data.description: Monsters of God is a jaw-dropping new series from the makers of the hit Netflix pandemic smash, exploring the murky world of exotic reptile smuggling In 1993, a sci-fi blockbuster about an animal theme park that resurrected the dinosaurs sparked more than a flurry of interest in those long-extinct beasts. It left audiences jonesing for the next best thing: a close encounter with a bearded dragon or a ball python. Jeremy McBride, the Emmy-winning film-maker was one of them. “I wanted a pet iguana,” he said. In the wake of the Spielberg classic, reptiles have become fixtures of the modern imagination, adorning zoo exhibits, living room terrariums and every corner of pop culture while underpinning a multibillion-dollar pet trade. But just as in Jurassic Park, the urgent danger isn’t the prehistoric creatures with the teeth and venom. It’s the people willing to steal, smuggle and kill for them. People like the Pablo Escobar of animal trafficking. “Our next documentary is going to be called Who Backstabbed Who,” jokes Eric Goode, an Emmy-nominated director. “You never know when that knife is going to go in your back because everyone’s trying to make a deal with the feds, with another reptile dealer. Even the good guys were supposedly doing bad things. It’s messy.” Continue reading...

data.title: British widow, 78, told to leave Sweden under Brexit rules after living there for 21 years
data.description: Authorities say application to stay was made too late, as UK officials say Sweden takes ‘stricter approach’ than other EU countries A 78-year-old British widow who has lived in Sweden for 21 years is fighting deportation from the country after authorities told her a post-Brexit application to stay had been submitted too late. Her case is the latest of 2,500 British people ordered to leave the country after Brexit in what campaigners and the UK’s Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) have said is an inexplicably hardline approach taken by the Swedish authorities. It comes two years after Sweden threatened to deport a British woman with dementia in a care home shortly before she died. Continue reading...

data.title: World’s seas have hit hottest temperature on record for July, say scientists
data.description: Average sea surface temperature outside polar regions was highest on record for July, beating previous high in 2023 The world’s seas were hotter last month than in any July on record, scientists have said, as devastating heat struck western Europe. Sea surface temperatures hit record highs for July on the Atlantic coast and western Mediterranean, the EU’s Copernicus climate change service found, with severe marine heatwaves roiling Europe’s seas. Globally, the average sea surface temperature outside the cold polar regions was the highest on record for the month, beating the previous July record set in 2023. Continue reading...

The tit-for-tat move came after Rome infuriated Madrid by launching checks on 1 August for travellers from Spain in response to the recent influx of about 72,000 people into Ceuta, a Spanish territory in north Africa. data.description: Guardian journalists have been uncovering cases involving US military personnel that bypassed British courts. It involved telling the stories of women who have been denied important rights and protections, and safeguarding them as sources Support investigative journalism today When reporters talk about protecting their sources, it isn’t always about protecting a source’s identity. Some sources are prepared to go public. Others may have already shed their anonymity before a journalist gets in touch with them. But they all still need to be supported and safeguarded as their stories are brought to light. “I try to ensure there are no surprises for them,” says Harry Davies, a Guardian investigations correspondent. “You have to prepare them for the exposure and talk them through what it will mean.” Continue reading...

data.title: The secret lives of theatre workers: ‘People were having full sex in the stalls’
data.description: Domestic dramas, bodily fluids, drink, drugs, rudeness and worse … ushers and box office staff have seen it all. So much for the myth of the ‘genteel’ theatregoer ‘Theatre still has a sheen of respectability, so people feel they can behave badly because where they are cancels out how dreadful they are being,” says John, who has been a box office manager for 15 years. From my early 20s to my mid-30s, I too worked in the box office, at some of London’s top theatres. During my decade in the job, I witnessed audience behaviour ranging from the odd and the outrageous to the outright belligerent. If you are under any illusion that theatre audiences are classy, allow my former colleagues to disabuse you of that notion. The misuse of phones is one of the most common offences. In April, Cynthia Erivo stopped her one-woman West End production of Dracula mid-performance to urge an audience member to stop filming. Former Love Island winner Amber Davies, starring in a tour of Legally Blonde, last month asked staff to kick out an audience member who was filming the performance from the front row of a Dublin theatre. And in May, Rosamund Pike spotted an audience member texting during the climax of her performance in Inter Alia. After the curtain call, Pike returned to the stage and shamed the behaviour , without singling out the culprit. Part of me hoped that, like a teacher, she would make the individual in question read their texts out to the rest of the theatre. Continue reading...

data.title: Broth, tart and salad: Kirk Haworth’s vegan tomato recipes for summer
data.description: A smoky tomato broth, a grilled peach, tomato and almond ‘ricotta’ salad scattered with roast almonds, and a sparky tomato tarte tatin August is peak tomato season. This most versatile of fruits can be put to just about any use, from raw to slow-cooked and from oven- or sun-dried to desserts (believe it or not, they go incredibly well with summer berries, especially strawberries and raspberries). Not only that, but tomatoes have high glutamate levels that rise even further as they ripen, which gives them an umami kick. However you prepare them, though, the key thing is never to keep tomatoes in the fridge: the chill breaks down their cell structure and, even more importantly, affects their flavour in an alarming way. data.title: My Brilliant Career: inside Netflix’s horny, ‘bonkers’ take on an Australian classic the world is about to love
data.description: Starring Philippa Northeast and an extremely buff Christopher Chung, Miles Franklin’s 1901 novel has been adapted into a spirited series ‘unashamedly intended for women’ Within the first 10 minutes of My Brilliant Career, Netflix’s new adaptation of the classic Australian novel by Miles Franklin, there’s smutty performance poetry and a Divinyls needle drop that suggests it’s not going to be your standard turn-of-the-century period drama. By the end of the first episode – in which our teen heroine, Sybylla Melvin, pops a squat for a bush wee and flashes her knickers at a drawing room full of toffs while dancing to a Rod Stewart cover – you sense that anything could happen. And yet somehow, the alfresco fingerbang later in the series still surprises. “It’s bonkers,” admits the show’s star Philippa Northeast, who plays Sybylla. “You really see this world through a teenage lens – which is true to Sybylla’s spirit and Miles’ age at the time she wrote the book … it reads like a teenager’s diary entry, pretty much.” Continue reading...

data.title: Game of Thrones: The Mad King review – an action-packed saga of dry ice and fire
data.description: Royal Shakespeare theatre, Stratford-upon-Avon This prequel to the TV series has one joust after another, spectacular stagecraft and plenty of modern resonance During the RSC’s 65 years, numerous Lears have lost their minds and frequent Caesars been slaughtered by their courts. Now, though, a tyrant new to its stages faces both fates. He is King Aerys II Targaryen, ancestor of one warring bloodline in Game of Thrones , the dramatisation of George RR Martin’s A Song of Ice and Fire series of fantasy novels that helped TV streamers’ rise to global domination during eight HBO seasons from 2011 to 2019. Some may balk at an institution named for England’s greatest dramatist staging an American drama franchise. There is, though, a compelling economic imperative: rising costs due to current wars (a frequent problem for Martin’s ancient oligarchs too) and Covid-era debts now exacerbated by paying back government loans means that the RSC could use another big commercial transfer – as its musical Matilda may not be immortal. Continue reading...

data.title: Centrist Democrats dismiss Abdul El-Sayed as a freak radical. Do they want to win in 2028 or not? | Nesrine Malik
data.description: Americans want someone on their side in the fight against vested interests – that means politicians like the Michigan primary winner and Zohran Mamdani Abdul El-Sayed’s win in the Michigan Senate primary was a historic breakthrough. Not only because he is a Muslim son of immigrants who broke with almost every single tenet of establishment Democratic party politics. But because he has wiped that complacent sneer at progressive wins off the faces of centrist gatekeepers. Zohran Mamdani? Relax, he’s just a mayor. And it’s New York City. Outside urban and liberal corridors, there is nothing to worry about. Now El-Sayed has won the Democratic party’s nomination in a swing state that is also on the list of presidential nomination states . There is a lot to be excited about. Not only within the US, but for observers abroad hopeful for the emergence of a truly revolutionary left that is able to weather powerful and well-funded adversaries and prevail. The money raised to defeat El-Sayed was staggering. He was outspent by more than nine to one. It was the most expensive Democratic congressional primary ever . A roll call of cartoon bad guys, such as Chevron and Philip Morris, funded his opponent, Haley Stevens, to the tune of over $60m. Of that funding, nearly half came from a Super Pac backed by the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac). Continue reading...

data.title: Subscriptions you can’t easily cancel, sales that aren’t sales – I’ll end the rip-offs that British people hate | Andy Burnham
data.description: These everyday hassles are small, but they add up – especially in a cost of living crisis. That’s why my government will tackle them head-on Andy Burnham is the UK prime minister Burnham vows crackdown on ‘rip-off’ business practices It’s remarkable how much of modern life can seem designed to wear us down. Every “ sale ” seems to come with an asterisk. Consumer contracts often find a way of costing more than you expected. And too many companies want you to sign up in seconds, but then make it feel impossible to leave. It’s exhausting. They might not be the issues that keep you up at night. But they’re often the reason you go to bed ticked off. Westminster has got used to telling people that these everyday hassles are just part of life. data.title: The idea of sin can cause shame and trauma. But what if it’s used as a cue to act? | Jackie Bailey
data.description: Instead of ‘being’ or ‘doing’ the wrong thing, a more useful understanding of sin may be of ‘missing the mark’ – a sense of not quite right-ness Making sense of it is a column about spirituality and how it can be used to navigate everyday life As a child, I was taught we are inherently unworthy of God’s love. “Forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us,” I would intone at Sunday mass, along with the other parishioners. I was imploring God, not just to overlook my theft of the last cookie in the pantry, but for something more fundamental. I asked him to remove the heavy weight of shame from my eight-year-old shoulders. I had absorbed the doctrine of “original sin” into the marrow of my bones, even though it was hard to square with another key teaching of my church: God is love. Surely, I reasoned, a loving God would not send me to hell if I failed to believe in Him? Jackie Bailey is an award-winning author whose latest book is The Outrageous Good Fortune of Living (HarperCollins). Jackie works as a funeral celebrant and pastoral care practitioner, supporting people to navigate death and dying Continue reading...

But there’s really nothing mystical about the dread and self-doubt they can induce As the new season of Ted Lasso started, I was reminded of one of the show’s stranger storylines. data.title: The Guardian view on India’s green growth gamble: it will need more than private finance | Editorial
data.description: The world’s most populous country needs state-generated demand to industrialise, decarbonise and avoid China’s overcapacity trap India is attempting to do something the world has never seen before. So claimed Niti Aayog, the government of India’s policy thinktank, earlier this year. It said that no major economy has tried to expand GDP nearly eightfold within a generation while simultaneously redirecting its energy and industrial systems to reach net zero within two generations. Hence its detailed report ’s claim that there is “no historical precedent”. There is something to this. China industrialised at vast scale, but not on a sustainable net zero path. Korea, Japan and Europe became wealthy by industrialising before decarbonising. Today, rich nations have already satisfied the basic demands of their people and created the infrastructure and high per-capita energy use that India is still trying to build. The world’s most populous country has to do this while also reducing emissions. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on the two cultures: bridge the divide, starting with A-levels | Editorial
data.description: Seventy years after CP Snow warned of estrangement between the sciences and arts, breadth in education should be encouraged After the playwright Tom Stoppard died last year, one of the most striking tributes to his work came from a clinical scientist. Michael Baum explained in the British Medical Journal how, in the interval of a 1993 performance of Arcadia, he experienced an epiphany . Thomasina Coverly’s attempt to plot the equation for a rose prompted him to realise that chaos theory was the best way to explain breast cancer’s pattern of recurrence. It was, he wrote, “the bond that links the arts and the sciences as one enterprise rather than the contents of two silos”. Mr Baum was not the first person to celebrate the bridging of this gap. CP Snow famously criticised the incuriosity of “literary intellectuals” about technology in his essay The Two Cultures (later turned into a lecture and a book). Whether or not this was justified at the time, many literary intellectuals besides Stoppard have since taken a close interest in science; Richard Holmes’s latest book, about the influence of evolutionary theory on Tennyson , is just one example. But the split between the humanities and sciences remains pronounced, and will be evident when this year’s A-level results are released on Thursday. Continue reading...

data.title: Tour de France Femmes: Vollering wins second title but tactics row rumbles on

data.title: Lake Mead plummets to historic low water level as Colorado River struggles
data.description: Levels at reservoir along Arizona-Nevada border dipped below previous record set in 2022, amid water crisis in west Lake Mead, the largest reservoir in the United States, has plummeted to its lowest water level since it was filled some 90 years ago, the latest sign of a deepening water crisis in the American west. Water levels at the reservoir, which straddles the Arizona-Nevada border outside Las Vegas, hit 1,040.4ft (317.1 meters) above sea level on Friday, according to federal data. That’s just below the record set on 28 July 2022, according to the US Bureau of Reclamation. Continue reading...

data.title: Falkland Islanders call for referendum on plans for massive salmon farm
data.description: The 3,500 population is divided over the venture, which would bring investment and jobs, but critics claim the environmental cost would be too high It is among the world’s last pristine wildernesses, with unique coastal waters rich in krill and squid that attract sea lions, elephant seals, dolphins and whales, and where penguins, of which there are five different species locally, outnumber people. But plans to make the Falkland Islands, one of the most remote and furthest-flung British overseas territories, a new frontier for salmon farming has split the 3,500-strong population. Now, people opposed to salmon farming are calling for a referendum because they have lost confidence in a consultation process they claim is biased towards the industry. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘You’re hit with a slam of shadow’: Nasa’s air mission to capture rare eclipse data
data.description: Two aviators will take off from Iceland to photograph the sun while flying at high altitude along solar eclipse’s path After lunch on Wednesday, two Nasa aviators will climb into a research plane and take off from Keflavik airport on a western tip of Iceland. They will climb north towards Greenland and then bank to head south on a gently curving course 40 miles (64km) off the Icelandic coast. Their mission can be described as chasing an eclipse, but in reality the eclipse is chasing them. As the plane cruises at 50,000ft (15,000 metres), the shadow of the moon will race up from behind, crossing the ocean below at more than 2,000mph (3,200km/h). The pilot will aim to reach the point of greatest eclipse, when the largest fraction of the sun is obscured by the moon, at the moment the shadow catches up with them. Continue reading...

data.title: Christine Borland obituary
data.description: Turner prize nominee whose installations, sculptures and films returned repeatedly to the histories embedded within bodies In 1994, Christine Borland, who has died aged 61 of cancer, opened her first solo exhibition at Tramway in Glasgow. Its starting point was a mail-order catalogue through which human skeletons could be legally purchased for medical teaching. The discovery that a person’s remains could be bought anonymously through the post gave rise to one of the defining questions of her career. Working with forensic experts, police and medical professionals, Borland attempted to reconstruct the life behind one such skeleton, producing a bronze facial reconstruction alongside the original bones. data.title: I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming review – brilliant bulletin from Ukrainian frontline dives deep into culture war
data.description: Locarno film festival A couple attempting to leave Ukraine when the war begins encounter gender identity issues in this bold and challenging film A movie’s themes could hardly be more urgent and contemporary than those on offer in this entirely absorbing film from German director Isabelle Stever and Ukrainian critic turned screenwriter Anna Melikova. It’s a bulletin from the frontline of Russia’s war on Ukraine, and from the culture war too. It is about identity and choices made in peacetime when less was at stake. There is a bold and brilliant premise that may at first look artificially satirical but is actually inspired. When Russia begins its attack, the crisis is very specific for a scared young Ukrainian couple, recently engaged: Olya (Tania Myronyshena) and Oleh (Markus Bright). As bombs rain down, they head west in the cramped car of Olya’s elderly mum and dad – with Olya grumpily objecting to her dad’s sexist comments from behind the wheel about female drivers – to stay with Olya’s sister, who is married with a young baby and whose husband, to her fury, has joined up. Oleh’s plan is to get out of Ukraine and live with Olya in the safety of Germany and the EU. Continue reading...

data.description: Touring her memoir and talking to others helped the author come to terms with her brother’s death, but the book’s success left her feeling guilty. Had she commodified her family’s pain? When my memoir about my life after my brother’s death was published, I was very fortunate that people connected with it. It’s not easy to feel good fortune from the worst thing that’s ever happened to you. But I suppose I felt pleased when the experience that had once made me so lonely suddenly became a point of connection. I had not always been an open book. I was 22 when my brother died from a rare bone cancer. The people around me didn’t know what to say about this awful thing, so they pretended it hadn’t happened and I pretended, too. For a few years I was a ghost in my own life. Nothing felt real. I got very good at imitating normality, imagining I was in a video game called Office. Continue reading...

data.title: William Orbit obituary
data.description: Musician and record producer who reignited Madonna’s career with his work on her 1998 album Ray of Light The career highlights of William Orbit, who has died aged 69, would run to several pages, featuring collaborations with Robbie Williams, All Saints, Prince, Kraftwerk, Britney Spears, Beth Orton and U2, but one of the most celebrated was his partnership with Madonna on her 1998 album Ray of Light. Coming at a point when Madonna had starred in the movie of Evita and had her first child, Lourdes, and her music career seemed to be waning, Ray of Light marked a decisive step into a new world of techno and ambient music. Orbit, who had previously made remixes of Madonna’s Justify My Love and Erotica , proved to be the perfect production partner, and Ray of Light’s blend of styles and textures made it one of Madonna’s most admired achievements, with 16 million copies of the album sold worldwide. data.title: Nas / The Roots review – NY rap legend is in a nostalgic state of mind
data.description: Crystal Palace Bowl, London Nas performs his gritty but intricate 90s classics, sharing the bill on the first London edition of the Roots Picnic festival with Questlove and co’s exuberant funk Looking out over the audience at the Crystal Palace Bowl, Nas feels moved to reminisce about his first visit to London. It was in 1994, around the time he released his landmark debut album Illmatic ; he remembers performing on pirate radio stations and “eating good Jamaican food”. It seems unlikely that he ever thought he’d be back in the capital sharing the stage with a man playing a sousaphone, but such is the power of the Roots Picnic, a US institution for nearly 20 years. Its famously eclectic bill has regularly featured great rappers backed by hip-hop’s premier live band, sousaphone player and all: Lil’ Wayne, the Wu-Tang Clan, Snoop Dogg, Jay-Z. Before Nas appears at the festival’s first London iteration, the Roots play their own set, augmented by a guest appearance from Common. It plays out almost as one long medley which shifts restlessly between their own back catalogue and old funk, soul and disco covers. They do a killer version of James Brown’s The Payback. Awesomely tight, driven by the relentless crack of drummer Questlove’s snare and heavy on jazzy brass solos, it’s a perfect demonstration of the unique musical space they’ve carved out over the years, somewhere between hip-hop and jam band: the Grateful Dead of rap, if you like. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘It’s rare to hear: I’m black and middle class’ – Symeon Brown on black Britain’s enduring ‘taboo’
data.description: Black people are more prominent than ever in the UK’s politics and culture. But are they overwhelmingly from the middle class, as Brown argues in his new book? And if so, why isn’t anyone talking about it? Symeon Brown and David Lammy went to the same primary school in Tottenham, north London. One went on to a selective secondary school, and became the second black person to hold one of Britain’s great offices of state. The other became a journalist who would go on to survey the country’s black professional class more thoroughly than anyone ever had – and who remembers being told by Lammy that he could “never become prime minister, because you sound like where you come from”. It was 2010, and Brown, interested in politics, was interning for the then Labour backbencher. “And he was right, certainly at the time,” Brown says now. Continue reading...

data.title: How to cook the perfect apricot galette – recipe | Felicity Cloake's how to make the perfect …
data.description: A free-form fruit tart that’s easy to throw together with whatever seasonal fruit you have to hand The galette takes its name from the pebble it’s said to resemble – as Elizabeth David observes, it takes many forms, all of them round and flat. For me the word conjures the buckwheat pancakes of Brittany while French friends, in a quick straw poll, tend to think first of the frangipane-stuffed puff pastry galette de rois served at Epiphany, with one vote for a buttery Breton biscuit. Ask the English-language internet, however, and you’ll be served what is more commonly known as a tart(e), more specifically a charmingly rustic, free-form version which doesn’t require a tin. Though Anne Willan references prune and apple three-tier galette pies from the Pyrenees in her 1981 classic French Regional Cooking, and David includes a yeasted version that sounds more like a cobbler in French Provincial Cooking, most fruit galette recipes I find seem to be American. My hunch is that Alice Waters’ tradition of a daily seasonal galette at Chez Panisse may have popularised the name across the pond, but the general idea never needed upselling. As a quick and easy way to turn a punnet of fruit into a dessert, it’s hard to beat, whatever you call it. Continue reading...

data.title: Recession nails or racial erasure? Why a ‘naked’ manicure is not as neutral as it seems
data.description: Bold colours are out and short, (seemingly) bare nails in, but some see trend as part of criticised ‘clean girl aesthetic’ Trends at Copenhagen fashion week are usually easy to spot. The so-called “fifth fashion week”, a laidback sibling to the other four main fashion cities, has previously popularised everything from romantic floaty dresses with practical trainers to giant hair scrunchies. But during its latest iteration that wrapped up on Friday, a much more subtle trend had emerged – naked nails. From the models on the catwalks to show-goers and passersby, fingers and toes featured short and unvarnished nails. The trend is a sharp shift away from the long, bright and glossy mani/pedis that have more recently dominated beauty standards. Continue reading...

data.title: We know sleep, exercise and diet are vital for health. But why?
data.description: The benefits of all three come down to a crucial piece of cellular kit Sleep. Exercise. Eat well. It’s the oldest recommendation in medicine, repeated so often it’s become a cliche. We know the advice, even if we don’t always follow it. But have you ever stopped to wonder why these three seemingly different habits have such remarkably similar effects on our brains and bodies? For generations we’ve treated them as separate prescriptions – sleep restores us, exercise strengthens us and food fuels us. Yet neuroscience is beginning to suggest something rather more elegant: they’re all essentially doing the same job. Continue reading...

data.title: Kindness of strangers: Leo drove us home in a blizzard, and his parting words have stayed with me
data.description: The roads were so treacherous that what should have been a five-minute drive took 40 minutes. My mum didn’t speak much English, so I did the talking Read more in the kindness of strangers series I was graduating from university the same day Storm Goretti was due to hit Birmingham. The forecast was for snow – and lots of it – so I decided to get the bus in, rather than risk driving and having to leave my car behind in a snowstorm. Joining me was my mum. We successfully attended the ceremony and managed to get on a bus back home but as the snow worsened, it broke down a kilometre from my house. The whole bus emptied and we were forced to walk through the blizzard. It was like The Day After Tomorrow out there. Tough conditions for anyone, but my mum, who was in her late 60s, was struggling to take even a few steps. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I’ve definitely lost followers’: influencers face backlash over Meta ‘pervert glasses’ content
data.description: Using ‘spy glasses’ made by Facebook owner leads to floods of negative comments, say content creators It was hardly an offensive video. Amid the buzz of the Tour de France finale, Oliver Hooson filmed himself whipping up a delicious-looking flat white for a fellow cycling enthusiast. But after posting the footage on social media, the comments that soon rolled in were a real shock. “PERV,” read one. “Out here pushing creep glasses,” said another. His mistake? Documenting the moment with Meta’s “spy glasses”. Despite being marketed as the latest must-have gadget, Meta’s smartglasses, which can record video footage while being worn, have faced a vicious backlash, particularly relating to concerns about surveillance. There are widespread fears about the glasses being used to film people, especially women, without their consent, and the resultant footage being posted on social media. This has earned them the label of “pervert glasses”, and content creators, no matter how they are used, have faced a flood of negative comments for deploying them. Continue reading...

data.description: Arthur Schopenhauer articulated a clear distinction between talent and genius, describing talent as the ability to achieve well-defined goals while genius encompasses a visionary perspective, identifying targets that remain hidden to most. This philosophical distinction is essential for fostering creativity and personal growth in contemporary contexts.

data.title: Quote of the day by Zhuangzi: 'Rewards and punishment is the lowest form of education'
data.description: The ancient philosopher Zhuangzi posited that rewards and punishments represent the most rudimentary form of education. He argued that relying on external controls stifles true human nature and impedes natural growth. Today, many educational systems still employ grades and fear tactics, manipulating students similarly to animals. Supporting this, Edward Deci's studies indicate that external rewards can diminish intrinsic enjoyment.

data.title: In 1987, Orlando put 1,200 acres of constructed wetlands to work cleaning reclaimed water
data.description: Orlando's constructed wetlands, established in 1987, treat billions of gallons of reclaimed water annually.  Aquatic plants absorb nutrients, but decaying matter creates sediment buildup over time.  Periodic earthmoving, known as demucking, removes this organic muck to restore marsh function.  This process involves draining, scraping, and replanting native species in 100-acre sections.  Such long-term maintenance ensures the wetland's continued effectiveness in water purification.

data.title: O populismo de crédito
data.description: Em 2022, às vésperas do segundo turno das eleições presidenciais, o governo Bolsonaro criou o crédito consignado para beneficiários do Auxílio Brasil , programa que havia substituído o Bolsa Família. Em poucos dias, a Caixa liberou cerca de R$ 8 bilhões em empréstimos, concentrados entre o primeiro e o segundo turno. Encerrada a eleição, as concessões foram interrompidas. A iniciativa era uma péssima ideia porque utilizava um programa de transferência de renda como garantia para empréstimos destinados a uma população vulnerável, por meio de um produto de crédito inadequado às suas necessidades. Leia mais (08/09/2026 - 22h00)
data.translatedTitle: Credit populism
data.translatedDescription: In 2022, on the eve of the second round of the presidential elections, the Bolsonaro government created consigned credit for beneficiaries of Auxílio Brasil, a program that had replaced Bolsa Família. In a few days, Caixa released around R$8 billion in loans, concentrated between the first and second rounds. Once the election was over, the concessions were interrupted. The initiative was a bad idea because it used an income transfer program as collateral for loans intended for a vulnerable population, through a credit product that was inappropriate for their needs. data.title: Supremo enfrenta o licenciamento licencioso
data.description: O Brasil vive nos últimos anos uma espécie de anomia programada crônica. A coreografia é conhecida : o Congresso Nacional , capturado por interesses particulares ou lobbies paroquiais, legisla contra os interesses do país. O Executivo tenta barrar os absurdos, é derrotado, e a matéria é levada ao Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), que se tornou o credor de último recurso da sanidade nacional. Não raro, ao tentar salvaguardar a Constituição, a corte ainda é tachada de "ativista". Leia mais (08/09/2026 - 22h00)
data.translatedTitle: Supremo faces licentious licensing
data.translatedDescription: Brazil has been experiencing a kind of chronic programmed anomie in recent years. The choreography is known: the National Congress, captured by private interests or parochial lobbies, legislates against the country's interests. The Executive tries to stop the absurdities, is defeated, and the matter is taken to the Federal Supreme Court (STF), which has become the creditor of last resort for national health. Not infrequently, when trying to safeguard the Constitution, the court is still branded as "activist". Read more (09/08/2026 - 10:00 pm)

data.title: Terapia com testosterona pode causar infertilidade?
data.description: A função da testosterona é, em grande parte, a produção de espermatozoides. É por isso que é um tanto paradoxal quando um homem que não precisa começa a tomá-la mesmo assim: seu cérebro registra um nível excepcionalmente alto do hormônio no sangue, conclui que o corpo produziu em excesso e envia a ordem para interromper a produção, o que faz com que os testículos fiquem inativos e a quantidade de espermatozoides diminua. Leia mais (08/09/2026 - 15h30)
data.translatedTitle: Can testosterone therapy cause infertility?
data.translatedDescription: The function of testosterone is, in large part, the production of sperm. That's why it's somewhat paradoxical when a man who doesn't need it starts taking it anyway: his brain registers an exceptionally high level of the hormone in the blood, concludes that the body has produced it in excess and sends the order to stop production, which causes the testicles to become inactive and the quantity of sperm to decrease. Read more (09/08/2026 - 3:30 pm)

Het is een van de bevindingen in een op Shell-documenten gebaseerd rapport van acht ngo’s. „Shell heeft zijn aandeelhouders misleid.”
data.translatedTitle: Internal documents show: Shell was aware of defects in the oil pipeline in the Niger Delta, but did not address them
data.translatedDescription: Shell deliberately continued to use a defective oil pipeline in the Niger Delta, which could cause large-scale oil pollution, contrary to its own code of conduct. It is one of the findings in a report by eight NGOs based on Shell documents. “Shell has misled its shareholders.”

data.title: Demi Vollering bewijst in Nice dat ze de Tourzege echt verdient, ondanks een tactische misser en een omstreden truc
data.description: Een tactische misser op de Mont Ventoux, een veelbesproken hindermanoeuvre van een ploeggenoot: de Tour van favoriet Demi Vollering verliep niet zonder hobbels. In de slotetappe bewees ze alsnog veruit de sterkste te zijn. Zo won de Nederlandse voor de tweede keer de Tour.
data.translatedTitle: Demi Vollering proves in Nice that she really deserves the Tour victory, despite a tactical mistake and a controversial trick
data.translatedDescription: A tactical mistake on the Mont Ventoux, a much-discussed obstacle maneuver by a teammate: the Tour of favorite Demi Vollering was not without bumps. In the final stage she still proved to be by far the strongest. The Dutch woman won the Tour for the second time.

data.title: Gigantische Lenin in Gronings graanveld torent uit boven theaterstuk ‘De Graanrepubliek’
data.description: ‘De graanrepubliek’, het boek van Frank Westerman, is door theatergroep Zummerbühne uit Groningen bewerkt tot een voorstelling op locatie. Midden in een graanveld in Oost-Groningen voeren ze het stuk op, met een bijzonder decorstuk: een negen meter hoog beeld van Lenin. Daar is niet iedereen blij mee.
data.translatedTitle: Giant Lenin in Groningen grain field towers above theater piece 'De Graanre republic'
data.translatedDescription: 'The grain republic', the book by Frank Westerman, has been adapted into a performance on location by theater group Zummerbühne from Groningen. They perform the play in the middle of a grain field in East Groningen, with a special set piece: a nine-meter-high statue of Lenin. Not everyone is happy with that.

data.title: Wat de ‘koopzegelrel’ zegt over de Nederlandse volksaard
data.description: Ik las het nieuws over de 'koopzegelrel' in 'De Stentor' die in een café in Lochem op tafel lag en wierp de krant van me af. Is dit wie wij zijn? Zijn het dan de koopzegeltjes die de inwoners van dit land op de barricaden krijgen?
data.translatedTitle: What the 'purchasing stamp riot' says about the Dutch national character
data.translatedDescription: I read the news about the 'seal stamp riot' in 'De Stentor' that was on the table in a café in Lochem and threw the newspaper away. Is this who we are? Is it the sales stamps that the residents of this country receive on the barricades?

data.title: ‘Een wondermedicijn is er niet, en toch neemt de kans af om dementie te krijgen’

data.translatedTitle: 'There is no miracle drug, and yet the risk of developing dementia is decreasing'
data.translatedDescription: A long-term population study in Rotterdam has taught Arfan Ikram a lot about the development of dementia. “I actually do the same job as Sherlock Holmes.”

data.title: Alleen de Patriot is effectief tegen ballistische raketten. Nu de voorraden opraken moet Oekraïne voorlopig toekijken hoe de Russen vrij spel hebben

data.translatedTitle: Only the Patriot is effective against ballistic missiles. Now that supplies are running low, Ukraine must watch the Russians have free rein for the time being
data.translatedDescription: Partly due to the Iran war, there is a worldwide shortage of Patriot missiles. Ukraine therefore has no chance against Russian ballistic missiles, which Putin can use in the war at will for the time being.

data.title: Waar kun je het beste kijken en heb je die eclipsbrilletjes echt nodig? En andere vragen over de zonsverduistering van woensdag
data.description: Voor het eerst sinds 1999 krijgt het vasteland van Europa weer een totale zonsverduistering. In Nederland schuift de maan komende woensdagavond voor 90 procent voor de zon. Het fenomeen is gade te slaan door een eclipsbril of online, maar kijk niet met het blote oog in het zonlicht: dat is schadelijk.
data.translatedTitle: Where is the best place to look and do you really need those eclipse glasses? And other questions about Wednesday's solar eclipse
data.translatedDescription: For the first time since 1999, mainland Europe will experience a total solar eclipse. In the Netherlands, the moon will move 90 percent in front of the sun next Wednesday evening. The phenomenon can be observed through eclipse glasses or online, but do not look into sunlight with your naked eye: that is harmful.

data.description: Ostatni taki bodziec rozwojowy miasto dostało w 1975 r., gdy utworzono województwo elbląskie. Kolejny jest teraz, dzięki budowie kanału i realizowanym przez nas inwestycjom. To dla nas brama na Bałtyk – mówi Michał Missan, prezydent Elbląga.
data.translatedTitle: Mayor of Elbląg: We have no intention of competing with the ports of Tricity
data.translatedDescription: The city received the last such development stimulus in 1975, when the Elbląg Voivodeship was created. The next one is now, thanks to the construction of the canal and the investments we have made. This is our gateway to the Baltic Sea - says Michał Missan, mayor of Elbląg.

data.title: Tajwan ćwiczy odpieranie chińskiego desantu, rosyjskie bomby spadły na Sumy
data.description: Przedstawiamy przegląd najważniejszych wydarzeń mijającej nocy: Tajwańskie wojsko symulowało odparcie desantu powietrznego Chin na wyspy Penghu; Rosjanie za pomocą kierowanych bomb lotniczych zaatakowali Sumy, raniąc pięć osób; na granicy Portugalii i Hiszpanii trwa walka z pożarami lasów, utrudniana przez upały; w Kolumbii zginął „Rosjanin”, jeden z dowódców partyzantów z b. FARC.
data.translatedTitle: Taiwan is practicing repelling the Chinese landing, Russian bombs fell on Sumy
data.translatedDescription: We present an overview of the most important events of the past night: The Taiwanese military simulated the repulse of China's air landing on the Penghu Islands; The Russians used guided air bombs to attack Sumy, injuring five people; forest fires are being fought on the border of Portugal and Spain, hampered by the heat; a "Russian", one of the former FARC guerrilla commanders, was killed in Colombia.

data.title: Ta meduza może żyć wiecznie. „Niezwykła sztuczka natury”
data.description: Niewielka meduza Turritopsis dohrnii potrafi w sytuacji zagrożenia wrócić do młodocianej formy i rozpocząć swój cykl życia od początku. Dzięki temu teoretycznie może unikać śmierci ze starości w zasadzie bez końca. To jedno z najbardziej niezwykłych zwierząt na świecie.
data.translatedTitle: This jellyfish can live forever. "Nature's Amazing Trick"
data.translatedDescription: The small jellyfish Turritopsis dohrnii can return to its juvenile form when threatened and start its life cycle from the beginning. Thanks to this, he can theoretically avoid death from old age indefinitely. This is one of the most unusual animals in the world.

data.title: Fico nie został nowym Orbánem Unii Europejskiej. Ale chciałby
data.description: Słowacja nie przejęła roli Węgier w blokowaniu sankcji wobec Rosji. Ale myślący o kolejnej kadencji premier Robert Fico łatwo poddaje się wpływom Kremla i Chin. A także dystansuje się od Donalda Trumpa.
data.translatedTitle: Fico did not become the new Orbán of the European Union. But he would like to
data.translatedDescription: Slovakia did not take over Hungary's role in blocking sanctions against Russia. But Prime Minister Robert Fico, who is thinking about another term, easily succumbs to the influence of the Kremlin and China. And he is also distancing himself from Donald Trump.

data.title: Waldemar Żurek: To my ogrywamy prezydenta, tylko metodami zgodnymi z prawem
data.description: Moim zdaniem moja pozycja jest stabilna i silna. Rozpuszczanie plotek o tym, że „Żurek jest do odstrzału” to próby utrudniania mojej codziennej pracy. Czasami nawet mnie to bawi – mówi „Rzeczpospolitej” minister sprawiedliwości Waldemar Żurek.
data.translatedTitle: Waldemar Żurek: We are beating the president, only using legal methods
data.translatedDescription: In my opinion, my position is stable and strong. Spreading rumors that "Żurek is ready to be shot" is an attempt to make my daily work more difficult. Sometimes it even amuses me, says Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek to "Rzeczpospolita".

data.title: Chopin i jego Europa łączy zwycięzców z najlepszymi orkiestrami
data.description: Sierpniowy Festiwal Chopin i jego Europa zdominują wielkie orkiestry i równie sławni pianiści jak choćby Vikingur Ólafsson. W porównaniu do lat poprzednich jest to zmiana, na którą z pewnością publiczność nie będzie narzekać.
data.translatedTitle: Chopin and his Europe combines winners with the best orchestras
data.translatedDescription: The August Chopin and his Europe Festival will be dominated by great orchestras and equally famous pianists, such as Vikingur Ólafsson. Compared to previous years, this is a change that the audience will certainly not complain about.

data.title: Znaki towarowe: podwyżki podatku nie będzie, o niższy trzeba walczyć
data.description: Skarbówka nie zgadza się na korzystne rozliczanie przychodów z dzierżawy znaków towarowych. Ale przegrywa z podatnikami w sądach. Z próby zaostrzenia przepisów też na razie nic nie wyszło.
data.translatedTitle: Trademarks: there will be no tax increase, you have to fight for a lower one
data.translatedDescription: The tax office does not agree to favorable settlement of income from the lease of trademarks. But it loses to taxpayers in the courts. So far, nothing has come of the attempt to tighten the regulations.

data.title: Lato na Krymie. Bez prądu, wody, paliwa
data.description: W środku lata na słynącym z turystyki półwyspie ludzie myją się  w wodzie z butelek i piorą w miednicach. W jednych miastach władze rozstawiają budki telefoniczne, w innych organizują kuchnie w podwórkach domów.
data.translatedTitle: Summer in Crimea. No electricity, water, fuel
data.translatedDescription: In the middle of summer, on the peninsula famous for its tourism, people wash themselves in water from bottles and wash their clothes in basins. In some cities, the authorities set up telephone booths, in others they organize kitchens in the backyards of houses.

data.title: Ameryce brakuje amunicji. Wojna z Iranem pochłania kolejne miliony
data.description: Administracja Donalda Trumpa temu zaprzecza, ale eksperci i media donoszą, że wojna z Iranem uszczupliła amerykańskie zapasy uzbrojenia do niepokojąco niskiego poziomu, prowadząc do znacznego osłabienia potencjału militarnego Stanów Zjednoczonych.
data.translatedTitle: America is running out of ammunition. The war with Iran is costing millions more
data.translatedDescription: The Donald Trump administration denies this, but experts and the media report that the war with Iran has depleted American weapons stockpiles to alarmingly low levels, leading to a significant weakening of the United States' military potential.

data.title: Marek A. Cichocki: Bez współpracy z Ukrainą Polska będzie bardziej zależna od Niemiec
data.description: Udajemy równego partnera Niemiec czy Francji, którym nie jesteśmy, a nie potrafimy stworzyć własnej pozycji regionalnego lidera. Polska musi podjąć własne starania o rozwój współpracy z Ukrainą – w swym naturalnym środowisku bezpieczeństwa i rozwoju, jakim jest Europa Środkowa.
data.translatedTitle: Marek A. Cichocki: Without cooperation with Ukraine, Poland will be more dependent on Germany
data.translatedDescription: We pretend to be an equal partner of Germany or France, which we are not, and we are unable to create our own position as a regional leader. Poland must make its own efforts to develop cooperation with Ukraine - in its natural environment of security and development, which is Central Europe.

data.title: Katarzyna Kęcka, wiceminister zdrowia: Strajk włoski lekarzy będzie mieć konsekwencje dla szpitali
data.description: W przypadku szpitali należących do sieci mniejsza liczba wykonanych świadczeń może przełożyć się na wysokość ryczałtu w kolejnym roku – ostrzega Katarzyna Kęcka, wiceminister zdrowia.
data.translatedTitle: Katarzyna Kęcka, Deputy Minister of Health: The Italian doctors' strike will have consequences for hospitals
data.translatedDescription: In the case of hospitals belonging to the network, a smaller number of services provided may translate into a lump sum payment in the following year - warns Katarzyna Kęcka, Deputy Minister of Health.

data.title: Koniec z botami udającymi ludzi. Banki muszą ujawnić, kiedy używają AI
data.description: Koniec z voicebotami udającymi żywych ludzi, niejasną automatyzacją i podszywaniem się pod banki za pomocą deepfake’ów. Przejrzystość algorytmów i bezpieczeństwo klientów stają na pierwszym planie.
data.translatedTitle: No more bots pretending to be humans. Banks must disclose when they use AI
data.translatedDescription: No more voicebots pretending to be real people, no more unclear automation and impersonating banks using deepfakes. Transparency of algorithms and customer security come to the fore.

data.title: Sponsorzy pompują rekordowe pieniądze w polski futbol. Piłka zostawia konkurencję w tyle
data.description: Futbol umocnił się na pozycji lidera rynku sponsoringu sportowego w Polsce. W ubiegłym roku wartość praw sponsoringowych wzrosła w tej dyscyplinie o ponad 32 proc. Spółki deklarują dalsze wsparcie dla klubów, rozgrywek i szkolenia młodzieży.
data.translatedTitle: Sponsors are pumping record amounts of money into Polish football. The ball leaves the competition behind
data.translatedDescription: Football has strengthened its position as the leader of the sports sponsorship market in Poland. Last year, the value of sponsorship rights in this discipline increased by over 32%. The companies declare further support for clubs, competitions and youth training.

data.title: Producenci gier jadą na Gamescom. Oczy rynku zwrócone na CD Projekt
data.description: 26 sierpnia ruszą największe coroczne targi gier w Europie i drugie co do wielkości na świecie. Wybiera się tam spora grupa firm z Polski. Oczy graczy oraz inwestorów zwrócone są m.in. na CD Projekt. Wiemy, co spółka zamierza pokazać na targach.
data.translatedTitle: Game producers are going to Gamescom. The market's eyes are on CD Projekt
data.translatedDescription: The largest annual gaming fair in Europe and the second largest in the world will start on August 26. A large group of companies from Poland are going there. The eyes of players and investors are focused on, among others, on CD Projekt. We know what the company intends to show at the fair.

data.title: Co piąty Polak będzie świętował Dzień Pracoholika
data.description: Chociaż tylko co piąty Polak uważa się za pracoholika, to ponad dwukrotnie większej grupie trudno oderwać się myślami od pracy, a niemal 60 proc. rezygnuje dla niej z odpoczynku lub prywatnych spotkań.
data.translatedTitle: Every fifth Pole will celebrate Workaholics' Day
data.translatedDescription: Although only every fifth Pole considers himself a workaholic, more than twice as many people find it difficult to take their minds off work, and almost 60 percent he gives up rest or private meetings for her.

data.title: Trump, CNN i TVN w jednej układance. Wielka transakcja może zmienić rynek mediów
data.description: Przejęcie Warner Bros. Discovery przez Paramount Skydance wciąż napotyka przeszkody, ale eksperci nie mają większych wątpliwości, że wielka transakcja dojdzie do skutku. Kluczowa rozprawa ruszy w marcu 2027 r., a jej wynik może wpłynąć także na przyszłość Grupy TVN i układ sił w polskiej telewizji.
data.translatedTitle: Trump, CNN and TVN in one puzzle. A big deal can change the media market
data.translatedDescription: Acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance still faces hurdles, but experts have little doubt the big deal will come to fruition. The key hearing will start in March 2027, and its result may also affect the future of the TVN Group and the balance of power in Polish television.

data.title: Tropy v Česku pokračují. Chladnější bude jediný den v týdnu, slibuje předpověď
data.description: V pondělí k večeru přibude kvůli přechodu slabé studené fronty oblačnosti a lokálně se přidají také bouřky, které mohou být ojediněle i silné. Předtím však budou znovu tropické teploty od 31 až do 36 °C. V noci na úterý srážky ustanou a obloha se postupně vyjasní. Za pondělní studenou frontou se krátce ochladí, ale teploty zůstanou letní. Ve druhé polovině týdne se pak postupně vrátí tropy.
data.translatedTitle: The tropics continue in the Czech Republic. Only one day of the week will be colder, the forecast promises
data.translatedDescription: Cloudiness will increase on Monday evening due to the passage of a weak cold front, and locally there will also be thunderstorms, which may occasionally be strong. Before that, however, there will be tropical temperatures again from 31 to 36 °C. On Tuesday night, the precipitation will stop and the sky will gradually clear. It will cool off briefly behind Monday's cold front, but temperatures will remain summery. In the second half of the week, the tropics will gradually return.

data.title: Roste už od poslední doby ledové, ale rychle mizí. Květinu se pokusí zachránit
data.description: Hvězdnice alpská, nápadně kvetoucí skalnička s fialově modrými květy a žlutým středem, se vyskytuje v severních Čechách na posledních třech lokalitách. Jde o kopce Bořeň a Sedlo v Českém středohoří a vrch Klíč v Lužických horách, kde má specifické podmínky k růstu. Aby z těchto lokalit definitivně nezmizela, spouští Agentura ochrany přírody a krajiny ČR (AOPK ČR) speciální záchranný program.
data.translatedTitle: It has been growing since the last ice age, but is quickly disappearing. He tries to save the flower
data.translatedDescription: Alpine star, a striking flowering rock plant with violet-blue flowers and a yellow center, is found in northern Bohemia at the last three locations. These are the Bořeň and Sedlo hills in the Český středohoří and the Klíč hill in the Lužické hory, where it has specific conditions for growth. So that it does not disappear from these locations for good, the Nature and Landscape Protection Agency of the Czech Republic (AOPK CR) is launching a special rescue program.

ner.entity: Nature and Landscape Protection Agency of the Czech
ner.label: ORG

data.title: Před požárem na západě Kanady prchlo 20 tisíc lidí, zemřela jedna žena
data.description: Při rozsáhlém požáru v kanadské provincii Britská Kolumbie zemřela osmdesátiletá žena, která se snažila utéct ze svého domu. Oznámila to podle agentury AFP kanadská královská jízdní policie.
data.translatedTitle: 20 thousand people fled from the fire in western Canada, one woman died
data.translatedDescription: An eighty-year-old woman who tried to escape from her home died in a large fire in the Canadian province of British Columbia. This was announced by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, according to AFP.

data.title: Ve zlatém dole u Marsa Alam v Egyptě se zřítila hornina, jeden člověk zemřel
data.description: Při zřícení horniny v největším egyptském zlatém dole přišel o život jeden pracovník a dalších pět bylo zraněno. Uvedla to agentura AFP s odvoláním na prohlášení egyptského ministerstva ropného průmyslu a minerálních zdrojů.
data.translatedTitle: A rock fell in a gold mine near Marsa Alam in Egypt, one person died
data.translatedDescription: A rock collapse at Egypt's largest gold mine has killed one worker and injured five others. This was reported by the AFP agency, citing a statement from the Egyptian Ministry of Petroleum Industry and Mineral Resources.

ner.entity: Ministry of Petroleum Industry and Mineral Resources
ner.label: ORG

data.title: Originál sochy Radegasta se bude stěhovat. Pohanský bůh získá vlastní svatyni
data.description: Originál slavné sochy Radegasta, který dnes stojí ve vestibulu radnice ve Frenštátu pod Radhoštěm, se bude stěhovat. Vedení podbeskydského města se rozhodlo najít pro něj nové umístění kvůli tomu, aby lidé měli větší šanci si ho prohlédnout.
data.translatedTitle: The original Radegast statue will be moving. A pagan god gets his own sanctuary
data.translatedDescription: The original of the famous statue of Radegast, which today stands in the vestibule of the town hall in Frenštát pod Radhoštěm, will be moved. The leadership of the Podbeskydy city decided to find a new location for it so that people would have a better chance to see it.

data.title: Plivance, nadávky i násilí. Křesťané v Jeruzalémě čelí nenávisti židů
data.description: Křesťané v Jeruzalémě čelí čím dál častějším nenávistným incidentům ze strany židovských náboženských extremistů. Ti na ně plivou, urážejí je a v některých případech je dokonce i fyzicky napadají. Pozorovatelé naznačují, že si nyní dovolují tak moc, protože mají zástupce ve vládě a stát jejich aktivity přehlíží.
data.translatedTitle: Spitting, swearing and violence. Christians in Jerusalem face Jew hatred
data.translatedDescription: Christians in Jerusalem are facing increasing hate incidents from Jewish religious extremists. They spit on them, insult them and in some cases even physically assault them. Observers suggest that they now enjoy so much power because they have representatives in the government and the state overlooks their activities.

data.title: Tuny vesmírného odpadu míří k Zemi. Stále častěji dopadají do obydlených oblastí
data.description: Zbytky raket a vysloužilých družic končí stále častěji po dopadu z vesmíru na polích, silnicích nebo dokonce v lidských domech. Zatímco do kosmu míří stále více raket a satelitů, mezinárodní pravidla pro odpovědnost za padající trosky vznikala v době, kdy je vypouštělo jen několik států. Určit viníka a získat odškodnění proto může trvat měsíce, případně k němu vůbec nedojde.
data.translatedTitle: Tons of space junk is headed for Earth. They are increasingly falling into populated areas
data.translatedDescription: The remains of rockets and retired satellites end up more and more frequently after impact from space in fields, roads or even in people's homes. While more and more rockets and satellites are headed for space, international rules for liability for falling debris were created at a time when only a few states were launching them. Determining the culprit and obtaining compensation can therefore take months, or may not happen at all.

data.title: I bezdomovec na tom byl líp než já. Lyžař Jan Hudec otevřeně o svém podnikání
data.description: Nikdy se nevzdává. Bývalý kanadský a český reprezentant v alpském lyžování získal na zimních olympijských hrách v Soči 2014 bronzovou medaili v superobřím slalomu jen měsíc poté, co mu vyhřezly ploténky a nemohl se vůbec hýbat. „Ve stejné době mi taky krachoval obchod a měl jsem posledních pár dolarů v kapse,“ vzpomíná Jan Hudec v rozhovoru pro iDNES.cz, pořízením na setkání investiční skupiny Rockaway.
data.translatedTitle: Even the homeless man was better off than me. Skier Jan Hudec openly about his business
data.translatedDescription: He never gives up. The former Canadian and Czech alpine skiing representative won a bronze medal in the super giant slalom at the 2014 Sochi Winter Olympics just a month after he suffered a herniated disc and was unable to move at all. "At the same time, my business was also failing and I had the last few dollars in my pocket," recalls Jan Hudec in an interview for iDNES.cz, taken at a meeting of the Rockaway investment group.

data.title: Roční iDNES Premium zlevňuje na 490 Kč. Čtenáři navíc získají 1 000 Kč na dovolenou
data.description: Sezona velkých letních dovolených pomalu končí, ale zkušení cestovatelé už plánují další výpravy. S novou nabídkou iDNES Premium mohou uspořit v rozpočtu a ještě získat zajímavé čtení. Mimořádné akce přináší roční předplatné za 490 korun místo obvyklých 989 korun a k tomu navíc přidává poukaz v hodnotě 1 000 Kč na nákup pobytu nebo zážitku přes portál Travelking.cz.
data.translatedTitle: The annual iDNES Premium is discounted to CZK 490. In addition, readers will receive CZK 1,000 for a vacation
data.translatedDescription: The season of big summer vacations is slowly coming to an end, but experienced travelers are already planning their next trips. With the new iDNES Premium offer, they can save on the budget and still get interesting reading. The special offer brings an annual subscription for 490 crowns instead of the usual 989 crowns, plus a voucher worth 1,000 CZK to purchase a stay or experience via the Travelking.cz portal.

data.title: Hypotéky dál drží růstový trend. Sazby vystřelily na dvouleté maximum
data.description: Hypotéky dál nekompromisně zdražují už pátý měsíc v řadě. V srpnu podle Swiss Life Hypoindexu vzrostla průměrná sazba na 5,42 % a dostala se nejvýše za poslední dva roky. Podle odborníků se úrokové sazby blíží svému vrcholu. K výraznému zlevnění hypoték ale nejspíš nedojde, lze očekávat stagnaci kolem současných hodnot.
data.translatedTitle: Mortgages continue to maintain an upward trend. Rates shot to a two-year high
data.translatedDescription: Mortgage prices continue to rise uncompromisingly for the fifth month in a row. In August, according to the Swiss Life Hypoindex, the average rate rose to 5.42%, reaching the highest level in two years. According to experts, interest rates are approaching their peak. However, it is unlikely that mortgages will be significantly cheaper, stagnation around current values ​​can be expected.

data.title: Léky za 1,7 miliardy končí v Česku v koši. Může za to špatná koordinace lékařů
data.description: V Česku se ročně zlikvidují léky za zhruba 1,2 miliardy korun. Další půlmiliardu korun lidé podle průzkumu Státního ústavu pro kontrolu léčiv (SÚKL) vyhodí do koše.
data.translatedTitle: Medicines worth 1.7 billion end up in the trash in the Czech Republic. Poor coordination of doctors is to blame
data.translatedDescription: Medicines worth approximately 1.2 billion crowns are disposed of annually in the Czech Republic. According to a survey by the State Institute for Drug Control (SÚKL), people will throw another half a billion crowns in the trash.

data.title: V Liberci hořel dům, evakuovalo se 15 lidí. Záchranáři ošetřili vyčerpané hasiče
data.description: Na libereckém Nerudově náměstí zachvátily plameny dvoupatrový dům. Podle zasahujících hasičů se událost obešla bez zranění, požár dostali před 19. hodinou pod kontrolu. Mluvčí Zdravotnické záchranné služby Libereckého kraje Michael Georgiev později večer upřesnil, že na místě ošetřili pět zasahujících, čtyři z nich byli vyčerpaní hasiči.
data.translatedTitle: A house was on fire in Liberec, 15 people were evacuated. Paramedics treated the exhausted firefighters
data.translatedDescription: Flames engulfed a two-story house on Neruda Square in Liberec. According to the responding firefighters, there were no injuries and the fire was brought under control before 7 p.m. The spokesman for the Liberec Region Medical Rescue Service, Michael Georgiev, specified later in the evening that they treated five responders on the spot, four of whom were exhausted firefighters.

data.title: S Íránem jednáme jen napůl, je to jako šachy, vždy to vyjde, prohlásil Trump
data.description: Írán se podle amerického prezidenta Donalda Trumpa dostává pod rostoucí ekonomický tlak. Prohlásil to po několika měsících války s blízkovýchodní zemí, která je dlouhodobě terčem amerických sankcí. Spojené státy navíc během konfliktu zahájily blokádu íránských přístavů.
data.translatedTitle: We're only half-dealing with Iran, it's like chess, it always works out, Trump said
data.translatedDescription: According to US President Donald Trump, Iran is coming under increasing economic pressure. He announced this after several months of war with the Middle Eastern country, which has long been the target of US sanctions. In addition, the United States began a blockade of Iranian ports during the conflict.

data.title: Neumíme změřit, jestli je žák dobrý. Školy nemají zpětnou vazbu, říká Daniel Prokop
data.description: O změnách, které se ve školství zavádějí, neumíme v Česku dost dobře říct, jestli mají dopad a tedy smysl. Státu totiž chybějí nástroje, jak to změřit a posoudit. Výzkumná organizace PAQ Research přišla s návodem, jak řízení vzdělávání zlepšit.
data.translatedTitle: We cannot measure whether a student is good. Schools do not have feedback, says Daniel Prokop
data.translatedDescription: In the Czech Republic, we cannot say well enough about the changes that are being introduced in education, whether they have an impact and therefore a sense. The state lacks the tools to measure and assess it. Research organization PAQ Research has come up with a guide on how to improve education management.

data.title: Obří loupež už 20 let fascinuje. Expolicisté ukradli 77 milionů, pak uškrtili komplice
data.description: Během chvíle bez jediného výstřelu zmizeli se 77 miliony korun a roky unikali před spravedlností. Od slavné „slavkovské loupeže“, jedné z největších v české historii, dnes uplynulo rovných 20 let a svým příběhem stále fascinuje.
data.translatedTitle: The giant heist has been fascinating for 20 years. Ex-police officers stole 77 million, then strangled accomplices
data.translatedDescription: Within moments, without a single shot, they disappeared with 77 million crowns and escaped justice for years. Exactly 20 years have passed since the famous "Slavkov robbery", one of the largest in Czech history, and its story still fascinates.

data.title: V dětství ochrnul, pak vyhrál olympiádu. Alois Hudec porazil árijce a znechutil Hitlera

This was announced on Sunday by the Syrian Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Damascus, which described the agreement as historic.

data.title: Na východě Číny udeřil tajfun Dolphin. Úřady evakuovaly přes milion lidí
data.description: Hustě osídlené východní pobřeží Číny zasáhl v neděli tajfun Dolphin. Úřady se na příchod bouře připravovaly několik dnů a evakuovalo se více než milion lidí z nejohroženějších oblastí. Zároveň se kvůli extrémnímu počasí zrušilo přibližně 1500 letů.
data.translatedTitle: Typhoon Dolphin hits eastern China. Authorities evacuated over a million people
data.translatedDescription: Typhoon Dolphin hit the densely populated east coast of China on Sunday. Authorities prepared for the arrival of the storm for several days, and more than a million people were evacuated from the most threatened areas. At the same time, approximately 1,500 flights were canceled due to extreme weather.

data.title: Místo lidí roboti. Britské sklady mají rozhýbat čínští šikulové
data.description: Velká Británie chce řešit nízký růst produktivity nasazením čínských robotů do skladů. Tyto technologie dnes pomáhají s přepravou, ale brzy mají zvládat i manipulaci a balení. Velký potenciál v automatizaci spatřují například přední výrobci elektromobilů.
data.translatedTitle: Robots instead of people. British warehouses are to be shaken up by Chinese chics
data.translatedDescription: Great Britain wants to tackle low productivity growth by deploying Chinese robots in warehouses. Today, these technologies help with transportation, but soon they should handle handling and packaging as well. Leading manufacturers of electric cars, for example, see great potential in automation.

data.title: Brutal Assault praskal ve švech. Primus, Wardruna i Ice-T ovládli Josefov
data.description: Brutal Assault znovu ukázal, proč patří mezi nejuznávanější evropské metalové festivaly. Letošní ročník přehlídky, který v sobotu skončil ve vojenské pevnosti Josefov v Jaroměři, nabídl během čtyř dnů více než 150 kapel a byl vyprodaný. Dramaturgie tentokrát vsadila spíše na pestrost než na komerčně známá jména. Vysoká návštěvnost je přitom pádnou odpovědí na debaty, zda festivalu nechyběli velcí headlineři, jakými v minulých letech byli například Gojira, Kerry King, In Flames či Behemoth.
data.translatedTitle: Brutal Assault was bursting at the seams. Primus, Wardruna and Ice-T dominated Josefov
data.translatedDescription: Brutal Assault once again showed why it is one of the most recognized European metal festivals. This year's show, which ended on Saturday at the Josefov military fortress in Jaroměř, offered more than 150 bands over four days and was sold out. This time, the dramaturgy bet on variety rather than on commercially known names. At the same time, the high attendance is a strong answer to the debates as to whether the festival lacked big headliners, such as Gojira, Kerry King, In Flames or Behemoth in previous years.

data.title: Piloval výcvik, ale i rozvíjel zeleň města. O co se v Olomouci zasadil maršál Radecký
data.description: V rakouské armádě už měl za sebou skvělou kariéru, když se v roce 1829 stal rakouský vojenský velitel a český šlechtic Jan Josef Václav Radecký z Radče hlavou olomoucké pevnosti. Jmenování mělo nádech vojenského důchodu, ostatně generál měl v té době 63 let a za sebou vítězství nad napoleonskými vojsky v bitvě národů u Lipska v roce 1813. Jeho olomoucké stopě se věnuje další díl seriálu iDNES Premium Tady psali dějiny.
data.translatedTitle: He honed his training, but also developed the greenery of the city. What did Marshal Radecký stand for in Olomouc
data.translatedDescription: He already had a great career in the Austrian army, when in 1829 the Austrian military commander and Czech nobleman Jan Josef Václav Radecký from Radč became the head of the Olomouc fortress. The appointment had the air of a military pension, after all, the general was 63 years old at the time and had won a victory over Napoleon's troops in the Battle of the Nations at Leipzig in 1813. The next episode of the iDNES Premium series Here They Wrote History is devoted to his Olomouc trail.

data.title: Černé vdovy v akci. Podvodné vydělávání na smrti vojáků prorostlo celým Ruskem
data.description: Ruské ženy uzavírají sňatky s vojáky jen proto, aby po jejich smrti získaly jako nejbližší rodinní příslušníci velké odškodné. Tyto „černé vdovy“ se často dostávají do sporů s rodinami vojáků, matky zesnulých je obviňují z podvodů před soudy i v televizních show. data.translatedDescription: Russian women marry soldiers only to receive large compensation as the next of kin after their death. These "black widows" often get into disputes with the families of soldiers, the mothers of the deceased accuse them of fraud in the courts and on television shows. But the authorities and military authorities are also involved in the extensive scheme.

data.translatedDescription: A bear attacked a cyclist in central Slovakia on Saturday evening. The fifty-five-year-old man, who suffered numerous open wounds, managed to walk himself to the nearest cottages after the attack, where he was called for help. He subsequently had to undergo surgery.

data.title: Poruchy příjmu potravy už jsou nemocí několika generací, říká psychiatrička
data.description: „Poruchy příjmu potravy se posouvají do nižších i vyšších věkových kategorií a stále častěji je vídáme také u mužů,“ říká psychiatrička Hana Papežová. V rozhovoru vzniklém u příležitosti otevření Centra denních stacionářů psychiatrické kliniky ve Všeobecné fakultní nemocnici popisuje, proč případů přibývá, jakou roli hrají sociální sítě a co je pro uzdravení pacientů klíčové.
data.translatedTitle: Eating disorders have been a disease of several generations, says the psychiatrist
data.translatedDescription: "Eating disorders are moving into younger and older age categories, and we see them more and more often in men as well," says psychiatrist Hana Papežová. In an interview created on the occasion of the opening of the Center for Day Outpatients of the Psychiatric Clinic at the General University Hospital, he describes why cases are increasing, what role social networks play and what is key to the recovery of patients.

data.title: Amélie z Montmartru ji nikdy neopustila. Audrey Tautou slaví padesátiny

Rodačka z Normandie, která 9. srpna slaví padesátiny, sice hrála třeba v Šifře mistra Leonarda nebo ztvárnila titulní roli v životopisném snímku Coco Chanel a od filmu si už nějakou dobu drží dostup, v srdcích lidí ale zůstává zapsána hlavně díky roli svérázné servírky.
data.translatedTitle: Amélie of Montmartre never left her. Audrey Tautou celebrates her 50th birthday
data.translatedDescription: Even today, the French actress Audrey Tautou remains mainly the famous Amélie of Montmartre, even though a quarter of a century has passed since the premiere of the film directed by Jean-Pierre Jeunet. The native of Normandy, who celebrates her 50th birthday on August 9th, played for example in Master Leonardo's Cipher or played the title role in the Coco Chanel biopic and has been away from the film for some time, but she remains in people's hearts mainly thanks to her role as a quirky waitress.

data.title: Není panelák jako panelák. Jaké má Most a jaké Polabiny? Vzniká virtuální kronika sídlišť
data.description: Zatímco pro většinu lidí jsou paneláky jen místem k bydlení, dvaadvacetiletý David Moravec z Pardubic v nich vidí mnohem víc. Se svým kolegou už za paneláky procestoval Česko i zahraničí a najel přes dvacet tisíc kilometrů. Dnes společně pracují na projektu, který má pardubické Polabiny vrátit zpátky v čase a přiblížit jejich historii nejen mladým generacím.
data.translatedTitle: It's not a block of flats like a block of flats. What is Most and what is Polabiny? A virtual chronicle of housing estates is being created
data.translatedDescription: While for most people, block of flats are just a place to live, twenty-two-year-old David Moravec from Pardubice sees much more in them. With his colleague, he already traveled the Czech Republic and abroad for block houses and drove over twenty thousand kilometers. Today, they are working together on a project that aims to return the Polabins of Pardubice back in time and bring their history closer not only to young generations.

data.title: Grupo japonês contra armas nucleares acusa Governo de querer alterar princípios não nucleares
data.description: O principal grupo japonês contra as armas nucleares, formado por sobreviventes dos bombardeamentos atómicos de Hiroshima e Nagasaki, assinalou hoje o seu 70.º aniversário com críticas ao atual Governo por tentar "alterar" princípios não nucleares do país.

data.translatedDescription: The main Japanese group against nuclear weapons, formed by survivors of the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, marked its 70th anniversary today by criticizing the current Government for trying to "change" the country's non-nuclear principles.

data.description: O Presidente colombiano, Abelardo de la Espriella, anunciou que seis membros de grupos armados foram mortos durante operações militares, nos primeiros dias de uma nova Administração que prometeu combater intensamente estas organizações e o narcotráfico.
data.translatedTitle: President of Colombia begins term with death of six members of armed groups
data.translatedDescription: Colombian President, Abelardo de la Espriella, announced that six members of armed groups were killed during military operations, in the first days of a new Administration that promised to intensely combat these organizations and drug trafficking.

data.title: O moçambicano que tornou moda cortar o cabelo em casa e até conquistou Geny Catamo
