data.description: O Partido dos Trabalhadores do Curdistão (PKK), em vias de dissolução, criticou um projeto de lei sobre o futuro dos seus combatentes que será submetido hoje no Parlamento turco, exigindo também a libertação do líder histórico da guerrilha curda.
data.translatedTitle: Kurdish armed group PKK criticizes proposed Turkish law on former fighters
data.translatedDescription: The Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), on the verge of dissolution, criticized a bill on the future of its fighters that will be submitted today in the Turkish Parliament, also demanding the release of the historic leader of the Kurdish guerrillas.

data.title: Temperatura média da superfície do mar atinge novo recorde em julho
data.description: A temperatura da superfície do mar a nível global no passado mês de julho foi a mais elevada alguma vez registada, anunciou hoje o Serviço de Alterações Climáticas do Copernicus (C3S) da União Europeia.
data.translatedTitle: Average sea surface temperature reaches new record in July
data.translatedDescription: Global sea surface temperatures last July were the highest ever recorded, the European Union's Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) announced today.

data.title: Governo de Taiwan planeia aumentar em 16% despesas com a Defesa em 2027
data.description: O Governo de Taiwan vai propor aumentar em 16% a despesa em Defesa para 1,1 biliões de dólares taiwaneses (29.5 mil milhões de euros) em 2027, informou este domingo a agência de notícias estatal CNA.
data.translatedTitle: Taiwan government plans to increase defense spending by 16% in 2027
data.translatedDescription: The Taiwanese government will propose increasing defense spending by 16% to 1.1 billion Taiwan dollars (29.5 billion euros) in 2027, state news agency CNA reported this Sunday.

data.title: Excedente da balança corrente do Japão cresce 22,5% na primeira metade de 2026
data.description: O Japão registou um excedente na conta corrente de 17,4 biliões de ienes (95,5 mil milhões de euros) na primeira metade de 2026, um valor 22,5% acima do registo homólogo anterior, informou hoje o Governo japonês.
data.translatedTitle: Japan's current account surplus grows 22.5% in the first half of 2026
data.translatedDescription: Japan recorded a current account surplus of 17.4 trillion yen (95.5 billion euros) in the first half of 2026, a figure 22.5% above the previous record a year ago, the Japanese government reported today.

data.title: Suspeito da morte do rapper Tupac Shakur vai a julgamento 30 anos após crime
data.description: O julgamento de um ex-líder de um grupo criminoso acusado de ter orquestrado o homicídio de Tupac Shakur começa hoje em Las Vegas, 30 anos após a morte do famoso rapper norte-americano.
data.translatedTitle: Suspect in rapper Tupac Shakur's death goes on trial 30 years after crime
data.translatedDescription: The trial of a former leader of a criminal group accused of having orchestrated the murder of Tupac Shakur begins today in Las Vegas, 30 years after the death of the famous American rapper.

data.translatedTitle: Typhoon Dolphin weakens after hitting eastern China

data.title: MAI diz que reparos do PR são alerta para se pensar e corrigir
data.description: O ministro da Administração Interna disse hoje que as chamadas de atenção e os reparos do Presidente da República são sempre vistos como uma forma de alerta e para se pensar e poder corrigir aquilo que há a corrigir.
data.translatedTitle: MAI says that PR repairs are a warning to think about and correct
data.translatedDescription: The Minister of Internal Administration said today that the President of the Republic's calls for attention and repairs are always seen as a form of warning and to think about and be able to correct what needs to be corrected.

data.title: Ambientalistas contestam central incineradora no Algarve
data.description: Consideram que a construção vai ter uma factura pesada para a região e que não é a melhor opção para a defesa do ambiente. A Zero vai pedir uma reunião de emergência à ministra do Ambiente.
data.translatedTitle: Environmentalists contest incinerator plant in Algarve
data.translatedDescription: They consider that the construction will have a heavy cost for the region and that it is not the best option for protecting the environment. Zero will ask the Minister of the Environment for an emergency meeting.

data.title: União das IPSS de Braga queixa-se a Seguro por causa do PRR
data.description: A União das IPSS de Braga enviou uma carta aberta a António José Seguro e ao Governo a alertar para o risco de perda de financiamento nos projetos do PRR na região. O setor social diz que há obras em atraso por responsabilidade das construtoras ou das demoras do próprio Estado.
data.translatedTitle: Union of IPSS of Braga complains to Insurance because of the PRR
data.translatedDescription: The Braga IPSS Union sent an open letter to António José Seguro and the Government warning of the risk of loss of funding in PRR projects in the region. The social sector says that works are delayed due to the responsibility of construction companies or delays by the State itself.

data.title: Piores incêndios lavram em Espanha
data.description: A vaga de calor que está a atravessar a Europa alimenta grandes incêndios florestais em toda a região mediterrânica. Desde o mês de maio houve já 1200 grandes fogos na Europa.
data.translatedTitle: Worst fires break out in Spain
data.translatedDescription: The heat wave that is crossing Europe is fueling large forest fires across the Mediterranean region. Since May there have been 1,200 large fires in Europe.

data.title: Europa debate-se com fortes níveis de seca
data.description: Em França, quase 70 departamentos estão sob fortes restrições de água, devido ao clima excepcionalmente quente e seco. Já foram ultrapassados os níveis mais críticos de 2022, tanto no solo como nos rios. No Reino Unido, os agricultores temem que a segurança alimentar possa estar em causa. Na Roménia, o exército continua a fazer explosões controladas para desviar a água do Danúbio.
data.translatedTitle: Europe struggles with severe levels of drought
data.translatedDescription: In France, almost 70 departments are under severe water restrictions due to the exceptionally hot and dry climate. The most critical levels of 2022 have already been exceeded, both in the soil and in rivers. In the UK, farmers fear that food security could be at stake. In Romania, the army continues to carry out controlled explosions to divert water from the Danube.

data.title: China em alerta máximo com chegada do Dolphin
data.description: A China está em alerta máximo para a chuegada do Tufão Dolphin, que atingiu as zonas costeiras. As autoridades retiraram mais de 900 mil residentes da cidade de Wenzhou e abriram mais de mil abrigos de emergência.
data.translatedTitle: China on high alert with arrival of Dolphin
data.translatedDescription: China is on high alert for Typhoon Dolphin, which hit coastal areas. Authorities evacuated more than 900,000 residents from the city of Wenzhou and opened more than a thousand emergency shelters.

data.title: Número de casamentos bateu recorde no ano passado
data.description: Nunca se casou tanto em Portugal. O ano passado teve o número mais alto da década, foram mais de 37 mil. Casa-se mais no norte do país e sobretudo pelo civil. Com vários preços, a média ronda os 25 mil euros.
data.translatedTitle: Number of weddings broke record last year
data.translatedDescription: He never got married so much in Portugal. Last year had the highest number of the decade, there were more than 37 thousand. They get married more in the north of the country and mainly in civil society. With various prices, the average is around 25 thousand euros.

data.title: Eclipse não tem o mesmo grau em todo o lado
data.description: Na próxima quarta-feira, os portugueses vão terminar o dia a olhar para o céu. O eclipse do sol vai ser visto em todo o território nacional, mas nem em todo o país se vai poder observar o fenómeno da mesma forma. Há uma pequena aldeia do distrito de Bragança onde o eclipse será total.
data.translatedTitle: Eclipse does not have the same degree everywhere
data.translatedDescription: Next Wednesday, the Portuguese will end the day looking at the sky. The solar eclipse will be seen throughout the country, but not across the country you will be able to observe the phenomenon in the same way. There is a small village in the district of Bragança where the eclipse will be total.

data.translatedDescription: Feirense received and drew 0-0 with Felgueiras, in the first round of the II League, in a match that was played in Vila Nova de Gaia, due to problems at the hosts' venue.

data.translatedDescription: Several regions of Ukraine came under fire and two people died. Kiev launched a drone attack on the city of Bolgorod that left five dead and 25 injured.

data.translatedDescription: Italian Jannik Sinner, leader of the world rankings, will not compete in the Masters 1,000 in Cincinnati, in the United States, which starts on Thursday, due to a problem in his right knee, the organization announced.

data.title: Mulher de 49 anos ferida com gravidade em colisão aquática no Alqueva
data.description: Uma mulher ficou hoje gravemente ferida e foi helitransportada para um hospital de Lisboa após uma colisão aquática no Alqueva, perto da Praia do Lago, no concelho de Moura, revelaram a Proteção Civil e os bombeiros.

data.translatedDescription: A woman was seriously injured today and was helitransported to a hospital in Lisbon after a water collision in Alqueva, near Praia do Lago, in the municipality of Moura, Civil Protection and firefighters revealed.

data.title: Piorou o estado de saúde do ex-presidente Joe Biden
data.description: O filho de Biden explicou que o ex-presidente norte-americano enfrenta uma fase mais difícil da luta contra o cancro da próstata.

data.translatedDescription: Biden's son explained that the former US president faces a more difficult phase in the fight against prostate cancer.

data.title: Confrontos com a polícia no Uíge fizeram 31 feridos, dez graves
data.description: Pelo menos 31 pessoas ficaram feridas, dez com gravidade, na sequência da intervenção da polícia junto à sede da UNITA no Uíge, no sábado, disse hoje à Lusa o secretário-geral da JURA, organização juvenil do partido, Nelito Ekuikui.
data.translatedTitle: Clashes with police in Uíge left 31 injured, ten seriously
data.translatedDescription: At least 31 people were injured, ten seriously, following the police intervention at the UNITA headquarters in Uíge, on Saturday, the secretary general of JURA, the party's youth organization, Nelito Ekuikui, told Lusa today.

data.title: Ataque `jihadista` a militares no Mali faz pelos menos 10 mortos
data.description: Pelo menos 10 militares foram mortos hoje numa cidade do centro do Mali, num ataque a um acampamento do exército, reivindicado por um grupo `jihadista` afiliado da Al-Qaida, segundo fontes de segurança e locais.
data.translatedTitle: 'Jihadist' attack on military personnel in Mali leaves at least 10 dead
data.translatedDescription: At least 10 soldiers were killed today in a city in central Mali, in an attack on an army camp, claimed by a 'jihadist' group affiliated with Al-Qaida, according to security and local sources.

data.title: Paulo Lino é campeão do mundo de Judo na categoria Síndrome de Down
data.description: Paulo Lino sagrou-se campeão do Mundo em atletas com Síndrome de Down no peso -60 kg. O judoca português conquistou a medalha de ouro na Suécia e levou a bandeira portuguesa ao lugar mais alto do pódio. Repete vitória de 2019. Também foi campeão da Europa por duas vezes.
data.translatedTitle: Paulo Lino is Judo world champion in the Down Syndrome category
data.translatedDescription: Paulo Lino became World Champion in athletes with Down Syndrome in the -60 kg weight. The Portuguese judoka won the gold medal in Sweden and took the Portuguese flag to the highest place on the podium. Repeats victory from 2019. He was also European champion twice.

data.title: Associação questiona elogios de deputado do PS à Rússia, partido nega apoio
data.description: A Associação dos Ucranianos em Portugal questionou hoje o PS sobre o deputado socialista José Carlos Barbosa que acusa de elogiar a Rússia numa viagem pelo país, mas o Partido Socialista refere que "não corresponde à realidade".

data.title: Saudi inflation remains contained at 1.8% in May: GASTAT
data.description:
RIYADH: Saudi Arabia’s annual inflation rate edged up to 1.8 percent in May with housing rents continuing to drive price gains in the Kingdom, official data showed. 

	According to the latest report released by the General Authority for Statistics, the Kingdom’s Consumer Price Index edged up 0.2 percent month on month in May, reflecting moderate increases across several categories, including food, housing and transportation.

data.title: Shanina Shaik is Australian fashion’s latest star
data.description:
DUBAI: Part-Saudi model Shanina Shaik is promoting a clutch of Australian brands on social media, starring in a campaigns after hitting the runway at Australian Fashion Week earlier this year.

	This week, she starred in a social media campaign for Dissh, a label led by creative director Lucy Henry-Hicks.

data.title: Israel says won’t withdraw troops from Lebanon, Syria, Gaza
data.description:
JERUSALEM: Israel’s defense minister said Monday that Israeli forces would remain in Lebanon, Syria and Gaza indefinitely, hours after the United States and Iran agreed to end the Middle East war, including in Lebanon.
	“Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and I are pursuing a clear policy under which the IDF will remain in the security zones in Lebanon, Syria and Gaza for an unlimited period of time, in order to protect the border and Israeli communities from there against jihadist elements,” Israel Katz said in a statement.

data.title: Saudi Arabia, South Korea sign MoU to boost oil and gas cooperation
data.description:
RIYADH: Saudi Arabia and South Korea signed a memorandum of understanding in Riyadh to enhance cooperation in the oil and gas sector and strengthen their broader energy partnership.

	Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman met with South Korea’s Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy, Kim Jung-kwan, in Riyadh, where the two sides reviewed areas of mutual interest and explored opportunities to expand energy investment and strengthen bilateral cooperation.

BEIRUT/JERUSALEM: Authorities in southern Lebanon warned people displaced by three months of war between Israel and Hezbollah against rushing home on Monday despite a US-Iran deal to end the wider conflict, as Israel said it would not withdraw troops from the south.

	The warning comes as Lebanon has not been informed of details of the US-Iran agreement, an official source told AFP on Monday.

	“Lebanon was not informed of the terms of the agreement or the time of the ceasefire,” the source said on condition of anonymity.

data.title: Gulf, Arab states welcome US-Iran deal to end war, reopen Hormuz
data.description:
DUBAI: Gulf and Arab states welcomed on Monday a US-Iran agreement to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, expressing hope that the deal will pave the way for lasting regional stability and broader diplomatic engagement.

	Saudi Arabia welcomed the agreement between Washington and Tehran to halt military operations and begin detailed negotiations over a 60-day period aimed at reaching a permanent settlement.

data.title: Norway crown princess’s son sentenced to four years in prison for rape: court
data.description:
OSLO: An Oslo court on Monday convicted Norwegian Crown Princess Mette-Marit’s son of two counts of rape, sentencing him to four years in prison in a high-profile scandal that has rocked the monarchy.
	Marius Borg Hoiby, 29, Mette-Marit’s son from a relationship prior to her 2001 marriage to Crown Prince Haakon, was accused of 40 charges, carrying a maximum possible sentence of 16 years in prison.
	He was acquitted of two other counts of rape and convicted of domestic abuse against an ex-girlfriend, issuing threats and traffic violations.

data.title: Oil hits 3-month low as US, Iran reach peace deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz
data.description:
SINGAPORE: Oil prices ​slipped to a three-month low on Monday after US President Donald Trump and Iran's deputy foreign minister said ‌they had reached an initial deal to end the war and to resume traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

	Brent crude futures fell $3.65, or 4.2 percent, to $83.68 a barrel by 09:30 a.m. and US West Texas Intermediate was at $80.75, down $4.13, or 4.9 percent. Both contracts fell to their lowest ​levels since March 10 on Monday after tumbling more than 3 percent on Friday.

data.title: Ahead of the Egypt–Belgium match, ambassadors exchange national team jerseys
data.description:
CAIRO: Ahead of Egypt’s World Cup clash in Seattle against Belgium on Monday in the opening match of Group G, the ambassadors of the two nations have exchanged team shirts as a sign of their “strong friendship.”

	The two nations have never met at the World Cup, but have faced each other in four friendly matches, with Egypt winning three.

	Several Egyptian players have played in Belgium, including Ahmed Hossam “Mido” at Gent, and former national team captain Ahmed Hassan and Mahmoud Trezeguet at R.S.C. Anderlecht.

data.title: Congo Airways : aucun avion opérationnel, la compagnie nationale face à de multiples défis
data.description: La compagnie aérienne nationale Congo Airways traverse une période particulièrement difficile. Alors qu'elle devait incarner la souveraineté aérienne de la République démocratique du Congo, aucun de ses avions n'est actuellement en exploitation. Les appareils de la compagnie sont immobilisés à l'aéroport international de N'djili, à Kinshasa.
data.translatedTitle: Congo Airways: no operational plane, the national airline facing multiple challenges
data.translatedDescription: The national airline Congo Airways is going through a particularly difficult period. While it was supposed to embody the air sovereignty of the Democratic Republic of Congo, none of its planes are currently in operation. The company's aircraft are grounded at N'djili international airport in Kinshasa.

data.title: Plus de 6 000 ménages déplacés assistés en articles ménagers à Lubero-Centre
data.description: Plus de 6 000 ménages de déplacés ont bénéficié, samedi 8 aout, d'une assistance en articles ménagers essentiels à Lubero-Centre, chef-lieu du territoire de Lubero, au Nord-Kivu. Organisée par la Croix-Rouge de la RDC avec l'appui de l'UNICEF, l'opération de distribution s'est achevée après une semaine d'activités.
data.translatedTitle: More than 6,000 displaced households assisted with household items in Lubero-Centre
data.translatedDescription: On Saturday August 8, more than 6,000 displaced households benefited from assistance with essential household items in Lubero-Centre, capital of the Lubero territory, in North Kivu. Organized by the Red Cross of the DRC with the support of UNICEF, the distribution operation was completed after a week of activities.

data.title: Reprise du trafic sur la rivière Lomami grâce à la remise en service provisoire du bac Makole
data.description: Le trafic a repris, depuis une semaine, sur la rivière Lomami après la réhabilitation du bac Makole, tombé en panne il y a plus de deux mois. Cette remise en service permet à nouveau aux véhicules et aux marchandises de traverser dans les deux sens entre les territoires de Kabinda et de Lubao.
data.translatedTitle: Resumption of traffic on the Lomami River thanks to the temporary return to service of the Makole ferry
data.translatedDescription: Traffic has resumed for a week on the Lomami River after the rehabilitation of the Makole ferry, which broke down more than two months ago. This reactivation once again allows vehicles and goods to cross in both directions between the territories of Kabinda and Lubao.

data.description: La Coalition Article 64 (C64) a condamné, samedi 8 aout, les attaques perpétrées contre des membres de l'opposition lors d'une réunion politique tenue le 6 août au Camp Luka ainsi que celles visant le siège de l'Engagement pour la Citoyenneté et le Développement (ECiDé) le 7 août dans la ville de Kinshasa.
data.translatedTitle: Article 64 Coalition condemns attacks on opposition and maintains August 15 deadline
data.translatedDescription: The Article 64 Coalition (C64) condemned, Saturday August 8, the attacks perpetrated against members of the opposition during a political meeting held on August 6 at Camp Luka as well as those targeting the headquarters of the Commitment for Citizenship and Development (ECiDé) on August 7 in the city of Kinshasa.

data.title: Lubumbashi : les commerçants du marché Mzee Kabila sommés de quitter les lieux avant le 20 août
data.description: Les vendeurs du marché Mzee Kabila, situé au centre-ville de Lubumbashi, ont jusqu'au 20 août prochain pour libérer le site et rejoindre d'autres marchés de la ville. Cette décision des autorités provinciales du Haut-Katanga s'inscrit dans le cadre d'un projet de reconstruction visant à ériger un marché moderne à l'emplacement actuel.
data.translatedTitle: Lubumbashi: traders at the Mzee Kabila market ordered to leave the premises before August 20
data.translatedDescription: Sellers at the Mzee Kabila market, located in downtown Lubumbashi, have until August 20 to vacate the site and join other markets in the city. This decision by the provincial authorities of Haut-Katanga is part of a reconstruction project aimed at building a modern market at the current location.

data.title: Plus de 137,8 millions USD issu de l’Eurobond déjà décaissés pour Grand Katende et les aéroports de N’djili et Luano ( ministère des Finances)
data.description: Le ministère des Finances a annoncé, jeudi 7 août, qu’un montant total de 137 894 270,17 USD issu de l’émission inaugurale de l’Eurobond de la République démocratique du Congo a déjà été décaissé au profit de projets structurants prioritaires. Selon un communiqué du cabinet du ministre des Finances, ces ressources ont été affectées conformément à la stratégie présentée aux investisseurs lors de l’émission de l’Eurobond.
data.translatedTitle: More than 137.8 million USD from the Eurobond already disbursed for Grand Katende and the airports of N’djili and Luano (Ministry of Finance)
data.translatedDescription: The Ministry of Finance announced, Thursday, August 7, that a total amount of 137,894,270.17 USD from the inaugural issue of the Eurobond of the Democratic Republic of Congo has already been disbursed for the benefit of priority structuring projects. According to a press release from the office of the Minister of Finance, these resources were allocated in accordance with the strategy presented to investors during the issuance of the Eurobond.

data.title: Sankuru : le Japon finance un pont sur la rivière Lotembo à Katako-Kombe
data.description: Le Japon a financé à hauteur de 352 500 dollars américains la construction d’un pont en béton armé sur la rivière Lotembo, dans le territoire de Katako-Kombe, au Sankuru. L’ouvrage a été officiellement inauguré le 6 août 2026 à Lumumbaville, en présence de l’ambassadeur du Japon en RDC, OGAWA Hidetoshi, et du ministre d’État au Plan, Guylain Nyembo.
data.translatedTitle: Sankuru: Japan finances a bridge over the Lotembo River in Katako-Kombe
data.translatedDescription: Japan has financed 352,500 US dollars for the construction of a reinforced concrete bridge over the Lotembo River, in the territory of Katako-Kombe, Sankuru. The work was officially inaugurated on August 6, 2026 in Lumumbaville, in the presence of the Japanese ambassador to the DRC, OGAWA Hidetoshi, and the Minister of State for Planning, Guylain Nyembo.

data.title: Au moins six morts et 31 rescapés dans le naufrage d’une baleinière près de Kisangani
data.description: Les recherches se sont poursuivies samedi 8 août afin de retrouver les personnes portées disparues après le naufrage d’une baleinière survenu jeudi soir, à hauteur du village de Linoko, près de Kisangani, dans la province de la Tshopo. Des sources locales parlent d'au moins six corps repêchés et 31 rescapés enregistrés, selon les dernières informations disponibles. Le bilan définitif reste difficile à établir, le manifeste des passagers n’ayant pas encore été retrouvé .
data.translatedTitle: At least six dead and 31 survivors in the sinking of a whaling boat near Kisangani
data.translatedDescription: The search continued on Saturday August 8 to find the people missing after the sinking of a whaling boat which occurred Thursday evening, near the village of Linoko, near Kisangani, in the province of Tshopo. Local sources speak of at least six bodies recovered and 31 survivors registered, according to the latest information available. The definitive assessment remains difficult to establish, the passengers' manifest having not yet been found.

data.title: Armwrestling: Golden Arms set for World Armwrestling Championship in New Delhi
data.description:
Ghana's national armwrestling team, the Golden Arms, will represent the country at the World Armwrestling Championship scheduled for October 26 to November 7, 2026, in New Delhi, India, as the Ghana Armwrestling Federation (GAF) steps up preparations for another major international assignment.

The championship, organised under the auspices of the World Armwrestling Federation (WAF), is expected to attract about 1,500 of the world's leading armwrestlers, providing the Golden Arms with an opportunity to compete against some of the strongest and most technically accomplished pullers from across the globe.

data.title: Génesis fue localizada por Interpol después de 20 días desaparecida
data.description: Tras permanecer 20 días desaparecida, Génesis María Ortiz Ramírez , de 11 años, fue localizada sana y salva por Interpol, poniendo fin a la angustia que durante casi tres semanas vivió su familia en San Pedro Sula . La menor había sido vista por última vez la mañana del 22 de julio, cuando salió al patio de su vivienda en la colonia Nuevos Horizontes para bañarse antes de prepararse para asistir a la escuela junto con sus dos hermanos. Desde ese momento, sus familiares desconocían su paradero y comenzaron una búsqueda con apoyo de las autoridades para establecer qué había ocurrido con la niña. Durante los días de incertidumbre, el caso generó preocupación entre familiares y habitantes del sector, mientras los investigadores realizaban distintas diligencias para encontrarla. La familia había denunciado haber recibido llamadas de personas desconocidas que exigían dinero a cambio de la supuesta liberación de Génesis. En una de esas comunicaciones solicitaron 50,000 pesos mexicanos y aseguraron que la niña se encontraba en México. Posteriormente, otra persona exigió 11,500 lempiras. Sin embargo, las autoridades habían informado que no existían elementos que confirmaran un secuestro y advirtieron que personas inescrupulosas podrían estar aprovechándose de la situación para intentar estafar a los familiares.
data.translatedTitle: Génesis was located by Interpol after missing for 20 days
data.translatedDescription: After remaining missing for 20 days, Génesis María Ortiz Ramírez, 11 years old, was located safe and sound by Interpol, putting an end to the anguish that her family lived in San Pedro Sula for almost three weeks. The minor had been seen for the last time on the morning of July 22, when she went out to the patio of her home in the Nuevos Horizontes neighborhood to take a bath before getting ready to attend school along with her two brothers. From that moment on, her relatives did not know her whereabouts and began a search with the support of the authorities to establish what had happened to the girl. During the days of uncertainty, the case generated concern among family members and residents of the sector, while investigators carried out various procedures to find her. The family had reported having received calls from unknown people demanding money in exchange for Génesis' supposed release. In one of these communications they requested 50,000 Mexican pesos and assured that the girl was in Mexico. Later, another person demanded 11,500 lempiras. However, the authorities had reported that there were no elements to confirm a kidnapping and warned that unscrupulous people could be taking advantage of the situation to try to defraud relatives.

data.title: "Nos encontraremos en el cielo”: el adiós y la súplica ignorada a Nasser Hilsaca
data.description: Un año atrás, Nalasser Hilsaca miraba desde una cama del Hospit General Atlántida y hablaba de volver a vivir. Este domingo, esa misma historia terminó frente a un féretro , entre oraciones, abrazos y el llanto incontenible de una hermana que permaneció junto a él hasta el final. A las 3:00 de la tarde, familiares y amigos acompañaron sus restos hasta la capilla del cementerio del barrio Mejía, en La Ceiba. Allí se celebró el oficio religioso antes de conducirlo hasta su última morada. Su hermana Básima Hilsaca allí tampoco se separó de él. “¡Ay, mi hermanito ya está descansando, ya está con nuestros padres. Nos encontraremos en el cielo, querido hermano!”, expresó entre lágrimas mientras despedía al hombre por quien durante meses pidió ayuda. La escena cerraba una historia que Honduras había conocido a través de imágenes difíciles de olvidar, pero cuyo drama iba mucho más allá de las 630 libras que llegó a pesar. Nasser tenía 58 años. Había nacido el 5 de julio de 1968 y comenzó a aumentar de peso desde su adolescencia. Sus padres, Isa José Hilsaca y Mirian Hilsaca, habían llegado a Honduras desde Medio Oriente y posteriormente establecieron a la familia en La Ceiba. Durante años fue comerciante y era conocido en el centro de la ciudad. Pero con el tiempo su obesidad y sus problemas de salud fueron reduciendo su mundo hasta prácticamente convertir una habitación en toda su existencia. Cuando llegó la pandemia en 2020, Nasser se instaló en un apartamento de un edificio de La Ceiba. La dificultad para desplazarse y el progresivo aumento de peso provocaron que dejara de bajar. Durante aproximadamente cinco años permaneció prácticamente confinado. El 23 de junio de 2025, su historia salió de aquella habitación. Bomberos, rescatistas y personal de apoyo protagonizaron durante horas una operación inédita para sacarlo del inmueble. Las escaleras no permitían movilizarlo, por lo que fue necesario utilizar una grúa y evacuarlo por la parte exterior del edificio. Las imágenes recorrieron Honduras : Nasser suspendido sobre una plataforma, descendiendo lentamente mientras decenas de personas observaban desde la calle. Hasta en el Hospital Atlántida hubo que improvisar. Tres camillas fueron soldadas para crear una superficie capaz de recibirlo y atenderlo. Pero detrás de aquellas imágenes había un hombre que todavía quería vivir. Días después del rescate, LA PRENSA conversó con él desde su cama hospitalaria. Estaba agotado, tenía dificultades para respirar, pero hablaba con esperanza. “De cómo entré a como estoy he vuelto a revivir”, dijo entonces. Agradecía la atención recibida y aseguraba sentirse mejor después de haber llegado en condiciones delicadas. Pero Nasser quería otra oportunidad. La solidaridad también apareció. Se organizaron actividades para recaudar fondos y ayudar con su atención, mientras su familia intentaba preparar una vivienda en condiciones que permitieran recibir a un hombre que necesitaba espacios especiales para poder entrar, movilizarse y utilizar un baño. Pero la mejoría no fue definitiva. Un año después, todo había cambiado. Para agosto de 2026, la realidad era otra. La enfermedad renal crónica se había sumado a las complicaciones provocadas por la obesidad mórbida. Nasser necesitaba diálisis periódicas y sus condiciones físicas hacían que cualquier traslado entre su casa y el hospital se convirtiera en una operación compleja. Su hermana Básima, también enferma y con serias limitaciones para movilizarse, se convirtió en su principal compañía. El viernes 7 de agosto, LA PRENSA publicó la que sería la última entrevista de Nasser. Ya no era el hombre que un año antes decía que había “vuelto a revivir”. Estaba cansado. Dolido.Y molesto. Aseguró que había recibido el alta médica, pero que seguía en el Hospital Atlántida porque no tenía las condiciones físicas ni logísticas para marcharse con seguridad. Básima explicaba que cada vez que lograban llevarlo a casa volvía a empeorar y tenía que regresar. “Es inhumano lo que estoy viviendo. Quieren que salga corriendo de aquí y ya no aguanto; solo saben decirme que ya no le pertenezco al hospital”, denunció Nasser. Su hermana tampoco tenía dónde descansar. LA PRENSA documentó a Básima durmiendo en el suelo después de que la cama que utilizaba fuera requerida por el centro hospitalario ante la falta de equipo. Ella misma necesitaba una silla de ruedas para desplazarse. Los dos hermanos permanecían atrapados en una situación que parecía no tener salida: Nasser necesitaba atención y diálisis; Básima no podía cuidarlo sola y movilizarlo requería equipo y ayuda externa. “Le dan el alta, pero no está bien”, reclamó ella. Su petición era conseguir una estructura o rampa que permitiera trasladarlo de una manera “digna”. Pero hubo un reclamo de Nasser que, después de su muerte, adquirió una dimensión todavía más dolorosa. En sus últimas declaraciones a LA PRENSA pidió algo elemental: poder estar limpio. Aseguró que no tenía facilidades para acceder al agua y asearse pese a permanecer prácticamente inmóvil y padecer lesiones en su cuerpo. “Eso es inhumano lo que están haciendo. Yo ya no aguanto”, dijo. Después agregó una frase que resumía su impotencia: “Estoy aquí. No tengo derecho a asearme”. Su temor era que la falta de higiene agravara las lesiones que padecía. “Es para que yo me siga pudriendo. No tiene que ser así”, reclamó. No pedía entonces una cirugía extraordinaria ni un tratamiento imposible de conseguir. Pedía agua, limpieza, asistencia y permanecer en un lugar donde se sintiera seguro. Su reclamo quedó registrado. Horas después, ya no habría tiempo para responderlo. “Siento que me ahogo”, exclamó. Y así fue. La mañana del sábado 8 de agosto, Nasser murió en el Hospital General Atlántida. Básima recordó después con LA PRENSA las últimas horas de su hermano. Contó que Nasser pedía constantemente que lo limpiaran y que le llevaran agua, pero que no contaban con suficiente personal para atenderlo. La mujer recordó una de las últimas expresiones que escuchó: “Déjame, ¿por qué no me dejas que yo me vaya? Siento que me ahogo, tengo calor”. Básima hacía lo que podía. Ella misma tenía dificultades para moverse. Aun así, se acercaba para acomodarle las almohadas, intentar aliviarlo y acompañarlo. “Yo no me podía mover del piso y él estaba enfermo, pero aun así le iba a colocar las almohadas. Murió durmiendo, parece”, relató. La familia cuestionó que, pese a las solicitudes que hicieron, Nasser permaneciera formalmente fuera de una hospitalización permanente y acudiera principalmente por sus tratamientos de diálisis. Básima reconoció también que el hospital argumentaba tener protocolos que debía cumplir. “Dios tiene la verdad y Él va a saber; ya mi hermano falleció y no vale la pena”, terminó diciendo. Hasta después de morir, mover a Nasser requirió de un esfuerzo extraordinario. Bomberos tuvieron que colaborar para retirar del hospital el féretro con su cuerpo, una escena que inevitablemente recordó aquel operativo que, poco más de un año antes, había permitido sacarlo de su apartamento para intentar salvarle la vida. Entonces descendía sostenido por una grúa y había esperanza. Esta vez salía dentro de un ataúd . Y este domingo, el recorrido terminó en el cementerio del barrio Mejía. Frente a su tumba quedaron Básima, familiares, amigos y una ciudad que siguió de cerca una historia marcada por la obesidad extrema, la pobreza de recursos para enfrentar una enfermedad compleja y una dependencia casi absoluta de terceros para las acciones más básicas de la vida. Nasser se hizo conocido por su peso, pero en sus últimos días pidió que lo miraran más allá de las 630 libras. Pidió poder movilizarse con dignidad. Pidió que no lo obligaran a marcharse cuando decía sentirse enfermo. Pidió que lo ayudaran a limpiarse. Pidió agua. Y pidió ser tratado como un paciente que todavía necesitaba ayuda. Un año antes había dicho a LA PRENSA que sentía que estaba “volviendo a vivir”. En sus últimas horas, la esperanza había sido reemplazada por otra frase: “Ya no aguanto”. Este domingo, mientras su hermana lloraba frente al féretro, la batalla terminó. “Ya está descansando”, repetía Básima. La Ceiba enterró a Nasser Hilsaca, pero su historia deja una pregunta que va mucho más allá de su enfermedad: qué tan preparado está el sistema de salud para atender con dignidad a un paciente cuya condición física exige cuidados extraordinarios, incluso para necesidades tan elementales como bañarse, trasladarse o simplemente sentirse acompañado.
data.translatedTitle: "We will meet in heaven": goodbye and the ignored plea to Nasser Hilsaca
data.translatedDescription: A year ago, Nalasser Hilsaca watched from a bed at the General Atlántida Hospital and talked about living again. This Sunday, that same story ended in front of a coffin, between prayers, hugs and the uncontrollable crying of a sister who remained with him until the end. At 3:00 in the afternoon, family and friends accompanied his remains to the chapel of the cemetery in the Mejía neighborhood, in La Ceiba. There the religious service was held before leading him to his final resting place. His sister Básima Hilsaca did not separate from him there either. "Oh, my little brother is already resting, he is already with our parents. We will meet in heaven, dear brother!" he expressed through tears while saying goodbye to the man for whom he asked for help for months. The scene closed a story that Honduras had known through images that were difficult to forget, but whose drama went far beyond the 630 pounds that he weighed. Nasser was 58 years old. He was born on July 5, 1968 and began to gain weight since his adolescence. His parents, Isa José Hilsaca and Mirian Hilsaca, had arrived in Honduras from the Middle East and later settled the family in La Ceiba. For years he was a merchant and was well known in the city center. But over time, his obesity and health problems reduced his world until he practically turned one room into his entire existence. When the pandemic hit in 2020, Nasser settled in an apartment in a building in La Ceiba. The difficulty in moving and the progressive weight gain caused him to stop losing weight. For approximately five years he remained practically confined. On June 23, 2025, his story left that room. Firefighters, rescuers and support personnel carried out an unprecedented operation for hours to remove him from the building. The stairs did not allow it to be moved, so it was necessary to use a crane and evacuate it through the outside of the building. Images spread across Honduras: Nasser suspended on a platform, slowly descending while dozens of people watched from the street. Even at the Atlántida Hospital we had to improvise. Three stretchers were welded together to create a surface capable of receiving and caring for him. But behind those images there was a man who still wanted to live. Days after the rescue, LA PRENSA spoke with him from his hospital bed. He was exhausted, had difficulty breathing, but spoke with hope. “From how I entered to where I am, I have come back to life,” he said then. He was grateful for the attention received and claimed to feel better after having arrived in delicate conditions. But Nasser wanted another chance. Solidarity also appeared. Activities were organized to raise funds and help with his care, while his family tried to prepare a home in conditions that would allow them to receive a man who needed special spaces to be able to enter, move around and use a bathroom. But the improvement was not definitive. A year later, everything had changed. By August 2026, the reality was different. Chronic kidney disease had added to the complications caused by morbid obesity. Nasser needed periodic dialysis and his physical conditions meant that any transfer between his home and the hospital became a complex operation. His sister Básima, also sick and with serious mobility limitations, became his main company. On Friday, August 7, LA PRENSA published what would be Nasser's last interview. He was no longer the man who a year earlier said he had “revived again.” I was tired. Hurt. And upset. He assured that he had received a medical discharge, but that he was still at the Atlántida Hospital because he did not have the physical or logistical conditions to leave safely. Básima explained that every time they managed to take him home he got worse again and had to return. "What I am experiencing is inhuman. They want me to run away from here and I can't stand it; they only know how to tell me that I no longer belong to the hospital," Nasser denounced. His sister had nowhere to rest either. LA PRENSA documented Básima sleeping on the floor after the bed she was using was required by the hospital due to a lack of equipment. She herself needed a wheelchair to get around. The two brothers remained trapped in a situation that seemed to have no way out: Nasser needed care and dialysis; Básima could not take care of him alone and mobilizing him required equipment and outside help. “They discharge him, but he is not well,” she claimed. Their request was to obtain a structure or ramp that would allow it to be moved in a “dignified” manner. But there was a claim by Nasser that, after his death, took on an even more painful dimension. In his last statements to LA PRENSA he asked for something basic: to be able to be clean. He assured that he did not have the facility to access water and clean himself despite remaining practically immobile and suffering from injuries to his body. "What they are doing is inhumane. I can't stand it anymore," he said. Then he added a phrase that summed up his helplessness: "I am here. I have no right to clean myself." His fear was that the lack of hygiene would aggravate the injuries he suffered. "It's so that I continue to rot. It doesn't have to be like that," he claimed. He did not then ask for extraordinary surgery or a treatment that was impossible to obtain. He asked for water, cleaning, assistance and to stay in a place where he felt safe. Your claim was registered. Hours later, there would be no time to answer it. “I feel like I'm drowning,” he exclaimed. And so it was. On the morning of Saturday, August 8, Nasser died at the Atlántida General Hospital. Básima later recalled with LA PRENSA her brother's last hours. He said that Nasser constantly asked for them to clean him and bring him water, but that they did not have enough staff to care for him. The woman remembered one of the last expressions she heard: "Leave me, why don't you let me go? I feel like I'm suffocating, I'm hot." Básima did what she could. She herself had difficulty moving. Even so, he approached to adjust the pillows, try to relieve him and accompany him. "I couldn't move from the floor and he was sick, but I was still going to put the pillows on him. He died sleeping, it seems," he said. The family questioned that, despite their requests, Nasser was formally kept out of permanent hospitalization and was coming primarily for his dialysis treatments. Básima also acknowledged that the hospital claimed to have protocols that it had to comply with. "God has the truth and He will know; my brother has already passed away and it is not worth it," he ended by saying. Even after he died, moving Nasser required an extraordinary effort. Firefighters had to collaborate to remove the coffin with his body from the hospital, a scene that inevitably recalled that operation that, just over a year before, had allowed him to be removed from his apartment to try to save his life. Then he descended supported by a crane and there was hope. This time he came out inside a coffin. And this Sunday, the tour ended at the cemetery in the Mejía neighborhood. In front of his grave were Básima, family, friends and a city that closely followed a history marked by extreme obesity, poverty of resources to face a complex disease and an almost absolute dependence on third parties for the most basic actions of life. Nasser became known for his weight, but in his final days he asked to be looked at beyond 630 pounds. He asked to be able to move with dignity. He asked that they not force him to leave when he said he felt sick. He asked for help to clean himself. He asked for water. And he asked to be treated as a patient who still needed help. A year earlier he had told LA PRENSA that he felt like he was “living again.” In his last hours, hope had been replaced by another phrase: “I can't take it anymore.” This Sunday, while his sister cried in front of the coffin, the battle ended. “He's already resting,” Básima repeated. La Ceiba buried Nasser Hilsaca, but his story leaves a question that goes far beyond his illness: how prepared is the health system to care with dignity for a patient whose physical condition requires extraordinary care, even for needs as basic as bathing, moving or simply feeling accompanied.

data.translatedTitle: Nasser Hilsaca now rests in his final resting place in La Ceiba, Atlántida
data.translatedDescription: In the midst of deep expressions of pain, family and friends said their last goodbye to Nasser Hilsaca this Sunday afternoon in La Ceiba, Atlántida. Around 3:00 in the afternoon, the body arrived at the cemetery chapel in the Mejía neighborhood, where an emotional religious service was held to entrust his soul to Christ before being transferred to his final resting place. data.title: Matan a padre e hijo y una mujer resulta herida dentro de su vivienda en Campamento, Olancho
data.description: Un ataque armado ocurrido este domingo 9 de agosto dejó como saldo la muerte de un hombre y su hijo , quienes fueron encontrados sin vida en el interior de su casa, situada en la comunidad de Piedras Amarillas, en el municipio de Campamento, Olancho. Las autoridades identificaron a los fallecidos como Germán Alonzo Torres , de 64 años, y Jerson Uriel Alonzo Juárez, de 33. Ambos fueron hallados muertos en el corredor de la vivienda, donde habrían sido sorprendidos por individuos armados que les dispararon. Durante el ataque, una mujer también sufrió heridas de consideración y tuvo que ser llevada de inmediato al Hospital San Francisco de Juticalpa para recibir atención médica. Su estado de salud es delicado y permanece bajo vigilancia de los médicos. De forma preliminar, trascendió que la sobreviviente sería esposa de Germán Alonzo y madre de Jerson Alonzo. Luego de conocerse el crimen, elementos de la Policía Nacional acudieron al lugar para acordonar la zona y comenzar con las investigaciones correspondientes. Los agentes trabajan en la recolección de indicios que ayuden a reconstruir la forma en que ocurrieron los hechos. Por ahora, no se ha determinado qué habría motivado el ataque ni existen detalles oficiales sobre quiénes estarían detrás del doble homicidio. De acuerdo con información preliminar, allegados a los fallecidos consideran que el hecho podría estar vinculado a algún conflicto previo con habitantes de la zona. No obstante, esta posibilidad aún forma parte de las líneas que deberán ser verificadas por los investigadores, quienes continúan recabando información para determinar el verdadero motivo del ataque.
data.translatedTitle: They kill a father and son and a woman is injured inside her home in Campamento, Olancho
data.translatedDescription: An armed attack that occurred this Sunday, August 9, left a man and his son dead, who were found dead inside their house, located in the community of Piedras Amarillas, in the municipality of Campamento, Olancho. The authorities identified the deceased as Germán Alonzo Torres, 64, and Jerson Uriel Alonzo Juárez, 33. Both were found dead in the hallway of the home, where they were allegedly surprised by armed individuals who shot them. During the attack, a woman also suffered serious injuries and had to be immediately taken to the San Francisco de Juticalpa Hospital to receive medical attention. His health is delicate and he remains under medical supervision. Preliminarily, it emerged that the survivor would be the wife of Germán Alonzo and mother of Jerson Alonzo. After learning of the crime, elements of the National Police went to the scene to cordon off the area and begin the corresponding investigations. The agents are working to collect evidence that will help reconstruct the way the events occurred. For now, it has not been determined what motivated the attack nor are there official details about who would be behind the double homicide. According to preliminary information, those close to the deceased believe that the incident could be linked to some previous conflict with residents of the area. However, this possibility is still part of the lines that must be verified by investigators, who continue to gather information to determine the true motive for the attack.

data.title: Video del momento de la balacera entre policías y civil en Olancho: “Mataron a mi hijo”
data.description: Un video captó el momento de la balacera registrada en la aldea El Tigre, valle de Lepaguare, Juticalpa, Olancho, donde un policía y un civil murieron durante un enfrentamiento armado. En las imágenes se observa a varios elementos policiales llegar hasta una vivienda del sector para realizar un operativo y buscar a una persona. Los agentes le ordenaron al hombre que bajara el arma, pero, según se observa en la grabación, este no habría obedecido la instrucción. Segundos después comenzó el intercambio de disparos entre los policías y el civil que se encontraba dentro de la vivienda. La balacera se prolongó por más de dos minutos y provocó momentos de pánico entre los pobladores que se encontraban cerca del lugar. En medio de las detonaciones también se escuchan los gritos desesperados de una mujer que expresó: “ Mataron a mi hijo ”. Tras el enfrentamiento murieron el agente policial Luis Humberto Licona y el civil Cristofer Colindres , quien, según reportes de medios locales, era jornalero. Medios locales también informaron sobre varias personas heridas, aunque hasta el momento no se han brindado mayores detalles sobre su estado de salud. Las autoridades investigan las circunstancias del enfrentamiento y esperan esclarecer lo ocurrido.
data.translatedTitle: Video of the moment of the shootout between police and civilians in Olancho: “They killed my son”
data.translatedDescription: A video captured the moment of the shooting in the El Tigre village, Lepaguare Valley, Juticalpa, Olancho, where a police officer and a civilian died during an armed confrontation. In the images, several police officers can be seen arriving at a home in the sector to carry out an operation and search for a person. The agents ordered the man to lower his weapon, but, as seen in the recording, he did not obey the instruction. Seconds later the exchange of shots began between the police officers and the civilian who was inside the house. The shooting lasted for more than two minutes and caused moments of panic among the residents who were near the scene. In the midst of the explosions, the desperate screams of a woman who expressed: “They killed my son” can also be heard. After the confrontation, police officer Luis Humberto Licona and civilian Cristofer Colindres died, who, according to local media reports, was a day laborer. Local media also reported on several injured people, although so far no further details have been provided about their health status. The authorities are investigating the circumstances of the confrontation and hope to clarify what happened.

data.title: ¿Cuánto ganan? CNBS vigilará ingresos de tiktokers y así reacciona Supremo
data.description: Los ingresos que generan tiktokers y otros creadores de contenido en Honduras podrían quedar bajo un mayor escrutinio como parte del fortalecimiento de los controles contra el lavado de activos que impulsa la Comisión Nacional de Bancos y Seguros (CNBS). Julieta Suazo, comisionada propietaria de la CNBS, explicó que la institución trabaja en reformas para ampliar las herramientas de prevención y detectar posibles operaciones irregulares a través de los distintos canales en los que actualmente se moviliza dinero, entre ellos las plataformas digitales. “Estamos fortaleciendo todo el sistema de prevención del lavado de activos, estamos muchos actores involucrados en eso”, manifestó Suazo, al señalar que iniciativas remitidas al Congreso Nacional buscan fortalecer el marco legal para combatir este delito. La funcionaria agregó que las investigaciones y mecanismos de prevención deberán considerar “todos los canales en que puede funcionar, incluyendo los tiktokers”, ante el crecimiento de los ingresos que algunos creadores aseguran obtener mediante redes sociales. Las declaraciones coinciden con el inicio, el pasado 4 de agosto, de la Quinta Ronda de Evaluaciones Mutuas del Grupo de Acción Financiera de Latinoamérica (Gafilat), proceso mediante el cual se evaluará la efectividad del sistema hondureño para prevenir y combatir el lavado de activos, financiamiento del terrorismo y otros delitos financieros. Sin embargo, una revisión realizada por LA PRENSA a las publicaciones oficiales de la CNBS no encontró, hasta ahora, un informe o comunicado que confirme la existencia de una lista de 26 o 36 tiktokers hondureños investigados, cifra que ha circulado en redes sociales y algunas publicaciones digitales. La discusión alcanzó a Supremo , uno de los creadores de contenido más conocidos del país, luego de que su nombre apareciera en publicaciones relacionadas con las supuestas investigaciones. El tiktoker negó tener vínculos con actividades ilícitas y aseguró desconocer quiénes estarían siendo investigados. Supremo ha revelado públicamente que sus ingresos provenientes de redes sociales rondan entre L700,000 y L800,000 durante un mes normal y que, en su mejor mes, habría alcanzado alrededor de L2.3 millones sumando sus diferentes plataformas. El creador sostuvo que los recursos que recibe provienen de su actividad digital y cuestionó la forma en que TikTok podría ser utilizada para lavar dinero. También aseguró que las instituciones bancarias han realizado controles cuando efectúa movimientos financieros de montos elevados. La CNBS, por su parte, sostiene que el fortalecimiento del sistema antilavado busca ampliar la capacidad del país para identificar riesgos dentro y fuera del sistema financiero tradicional, en momentos en que las plataformas digitales permiten movilizar nuevas fuentes y volúmenes de ingresos.
data.translatedTitle: How much do they earn? CNBS will monitor income from tiktokers and this is how Supremo reacts
data.translatedDescription: The income generated by TikTokers and other content creators in Honduras could come under greater scrutiny as part of the strengthening of anti-money laundering controls promoted by the National Banking and Insurance Commission (CNBS). Julieta Suazo, commissioner who owns the CNBS, explained that the institution is working on reforms to expand prevention tools and detect possible irregular operations through the different channels in which money is currently mobilized, including digital platforms. “We are strengthening the entire money laundering prevention system, there are many actors involved in that,” said Suazo, noting that initiatives sent to the National Congress seek to strengthen the legal framework to combat this crime. The official added that investigations and prevention mechanisms must consider “all the channels in which it can operate, including TikTok,” given the growth in income that some creators claim to obtain through social networks. The statements coincide with the beginning, on August 4, of the Fifth Round of Mutual Evaluations of the Latin American Financial Action Group (Gafilat), a process through which the effectiveness of the Honduran system to prevent and combat money laundering, terrorist financing and other financial crimes will be evaluated. However, a review carried out by LA PRENSA of the official publications of the CNBS did not find, until now, a report or statement that confirms the existence of a list of 26 or 36 Honduran tiktokers investigated, a figure that has circulated on social networks and some digital publications. The discussion reached Supremo, one of the country's best-known content creators, after his name appeared in publications related to the alleged investigations. The tiktoker denied having links to illicit activities and claimed not to know who was being investigated. Supremo has publicly revealed that its income from social networks is between L700,000 and L800,000 during a normal month and that, in its best month, it would have reached around L2.3 million adding its different platforms. The creator maintained that the resources he receives come from his digital activity and questioned the way in which TikTok could be used to launder money. He also assured that banking institutions have carried out controls when carrying out financial movements of large amounts. The CNBS, for its part, maintains that the strengthening of the anti-laundering system seeks to expand the country's capacity to identify risks inside and outside the traditional financial system, at a time when digital platforms allow new sources and volumes of income to be mobilized.

data.title: Gorgojo descortezador amenaza los bosques: afecta casi 300 hectáreas en 2026
data.description: El gorgojo descortezador continúa afectando cada año los bosques de pino del país. En 2026, la sequía y las altas temperaturas que se registran en gran parte del territorio favorecen la propagación de esta plaga, debido a que estas condiciones debilitan los árboles y los hacen más vulnerables. Datos oficiales del Instituto de Conservación Forestal ( ICF ) reflejan que, en lo que va del año, se contabilizan 414 reportes de la plaga, que ya ha afectado 296.89 hectáreas. Las zonas con mayor concentración se encuentran en el departamento de Yoro , seguido de Lempira y El Paraíso, además de otras regiones del occidente del país. De acuerdo con los registros comparativos, el comportamiento de la plaga ha mostrado variaciones en los últimos años. Aunque en 2026 el número de reportes es menor, el área afectada casi iguala a la registrada en años anteriores. En 2021 se reportaron 498 incidencias y 368.88 hectáreas dañadas. En 2022, la cifra se disparó a 1,164 reportes, con 425.67 hectáreas afectadas. Para 2023, los reportes bajaron a 1,033, con 247.95 hectáreas afectadas, mientras que en 2024 se registraron 975 reportes y 350.54 hectáreas. En 2025 hubo una reducción significativa, con 371 reportes y 220.07 hectáreas, pero en 2026 se observa un repunte en el área afectada, aunque con menos incidencias que en los años críticos. Este comportamiento evidencia que, si bien los brotes pueden ser contenidos en número, la extensión del daño continúa siendo una amenaza latente, especialmente bajo condiciones climáticas adversas. El dasónomo Manuel Izaguirre explicó a EL HERALDO que la propagación del gorgojo está directamente relacionada con el estrés hídrico de los bosques. Las altas temperaturas y la falta de lluvias debilitan los árboles y facilitan que el gorgojo ataque de forma masiva, detalló. Según el experto, la combinación de sequía, incendios forestales y bajas precipitaciones crea el escenario ideal para la proliferación de esta plaga. "Los árboles debilitados por el fuego o la falta de agua son más vulnerables, y ahí es donde el gorgojo encuentra las condiciones para expandirse rápidamente", indicó. Los datos de la plataforma Sigmof del ICF muestran que este año el pino ocotea (Pinus oocarpa) es la especie más afectada y concentra la mayor parte del área dañada. Asimismo, el principal agente identificado es el insecto del género Ips (gorgojo descortezador), responsable de la mayor parte de la destrucción forestal. A nivel territorial, Yoro encabeza la lista de departamentos con mayor extensión afectada, al superar las 100 hectáreas. Le siguen municipios como Jocón, Yoro; La Campa, Lempira, y San Luis, Santa Bárbara, donde la incidencia ha sido constante. Izaguirre advirtió que, de mantenerse las actuales condiciones climáticas, el panorama podría agravarse. "Si no hay lluvias suficientes, el escenario es crítico, porque la plaga puede seguir reproduciéndose y expandiéndose en los bosques de pino", señaló. Sin embargo, el país aún está a tiempo de evitar un brote de gran escala como el ocurrido entre 2013 y 2016, cuando se perdieron más de 500,000 hectáreas de bosque, señaló el experto. El control del gorgojo descortezador se basa principalmente en la intervención directa sobre los árboles infestados. Estela Mejía , subdirectora de Manejo y Desarrollo Forestal del ICF, indicó que la única forma de parar al gorgojo es mediante el corte de los árboles afectados. "Si no se corta el árbol, no se detiene el ataque del gorgojo", dijo. Además del gorgojo, otras plagas, como la langosta, están afectando los bosques, aunque su impacto tiende a disminuir con la llegada de las lluvias, a diferencia del descortezador, que puede mantenerse activo durante todo el año si las condiciones le son favorables. Las autoridades y los expertos coinciden en que la llegada de lluvias intensas y sostenidas podría reducir la incidencia de la plaga, al mejorar las condiciones de los árboles y limitar la reproducción del insecto.
data.translatedTitle: Bark weevil threatens forests: it will affect almost 300 hectares in 2026
data.translatedDescription: The bark weevil continues to affect the country's pine forests every year. In 2026, the drought and high temperatures recorded in much of the territory favor the spread of this pest, because these conditions weaken the trees and make them more vulnerable. Official data from the Forest Conservation Institute (ICF) reflect that, so far this year, there have been 414 reports of the pest, which has already affected 296.89 hectares. The areas with the highest concentration are in the department of Yoro, followed by Lempira and El Paraíso, as well as other regions in the west of the country. According to comparative records, the behavior of the pest has shown variations in recent years. Although in 2026 the number of reports is lower, the affected area is almost equal to that registered in previous years. In 2021, 498 incidents were reported and 368.88 hectares damaged. In 2022, the figure skyrocketed to 1,164 reports, with 425.67 hectares affected. By 2023, reports dropped to 1,033, with 247.95 hectares affected, while in 2024, 975 reports and 350.54 hectares were recorded. In 2025 there was a significant reduction, with 371 reports and 220.07 hectares, but in 2026 a rebound is observed in the affected area, although with fewer incidents than in critical years. This behavior shows that, although outbreaks can be contained in number, the extent of damage continues to be a latent threat, especially under adverse climatic conditions. Forester Manuel Izaguirre explained to EL HERALDO that the spread of the weevil is directly related to water stress in forests. High temperatures and lack of rain weaken the trees and make it easier for the weevil to attack en masse, he explained. According to the expert, the combination of drought, forest fires and low rainfall creates the ideal scenario for the proliferation of this pest. "Trees weakened by fire or lack of water are more vulnerable, and that is where the weevil finds the conditions to expand rapidly," he said. Data from the ICF's Sigmof platform show that this year the ocotea pine (Pinus oocarpa) is the most affected species and concentrates most of the damaged area. Likewise, the main agent identified is the insect of the genus Ips (bark weevil), responsible for most of the forest destruction. At the territorial level, Yoro heads the list of departments with the largest affected area, exceeding 100 hectares. It is followed by municipalities such as Jocón, Yoro; La Campa, Lempira, and San Luis, Santa Bárbara, where the incidence has been constant. Izaguirre warned that, if current weather conditions continue, the situation could worsen. "If there is not enough rain, the scenario is critical, because the pest can continue to reproduce and expand in the pine forests," he said. However, the country still has time to avoid a large-scale outbreak like the one that occurred between 2013 and 2016, when more than 500,000 hectares of forest were lost, the expert said. Control of the bark weevil is mainly based on direct intervention on infested trees. Estela Mejía, deputy director of Forest Management and Development at the ICF, indicated that the only way to stop the weevil is by cutting down the affected trees. "If you don't cut the tree, you don't stop the weevil attack," he said. In addition to the weevil, other pests, such as the locust, are affecting the forests, although their impact tends to decrease with the arrival of the rains, unlike the bark beetle, which can remain active throughout the year if conditions are favorable. Authorities and experts agree that the arrival of intense and sustained rains could reduce the incidence of the pest, by improving the conditions of the trees and limiting the reproduction of the insect.
