data.title: Selección de Grandes Crímenes: La lista del padre Santos (Primera parte)
data.description: PERROS. El camino estaba húmedo. Era un camino real, bordeado de árboles que se alzaban detrás de un largo y viejo muro de piedra. Más allá crecían las milpas verdes, llenas de vida, con elotes hermosos de largas cabelleras de oro. Al otro lado pastaba el ganado en un potrero que se alejaba hasta perderse con el bosque que empezaba al pie de las montañas. Era temprano, el sol asomaba a lo lejos y subía despacio bajo un cielo gris que empezaba a cargarse de lluvia. Nada más bello que el campo, pero cuando parece un paraíso y no la escena de un crimen tan horrible como detestable. Detrás de una roca enorme, rodeada de arbustos, estaban tres perros grandes y furiosos que gruñían, ladrando y enseñándose unos a otros los largos colmillos, manchados con sangre fresca. Comían y se peleaban por la comida que acababan de desenterrar de una especie de tumba improvisada que alguien había excavado entre la roca y el muro, donde la tierra era más blanda y estaba cubierta por las ramas tupidas de los arbustos. Desgarraban masticaba, tragaban y se lanzaban dentelladas entre ellos. Uno se comía un bracito, triturando con hambre los huesos; el segundo arrancaba lo que quedaba de una pequeña pierna y el diminuto pie, mientras el tercero se atascaba con las entrañas que seguían unidas a un largo cordón umbilical. A un lado estaba una cabecita llena de sangre y tierra, ya separada del pequeño tronco, que pronto desaparecería entre los voraces hocicos de los perros. ¿Cómo habían encontrado aquel siniestro festín? Pues nadie podría decirlo. Se veía que escarbaron con desesperación, esa que provoca el hambre, y juntos sacaron de aquella fosa los restos que engullían a grandes tarascadas. Por supuesto, aquel era un potrero no un cementerio, y lo que comían los perros era lo que quedaba de un feto, tal vez un niño recién nacido que alguien no quiso que viniera al mundo. Don Arcadio se bajó del caballo. Desde aquella altura se veía sobre el muro lo que estaba pasando cerca de la roca. Sacó su revólver de la cintura e hizo dos disparos al aire. Los perros más hambrientos que asustados lo vieron goteando sangre de entre los dientes y uno de ellos se atrevió a gruñir, desafiante. Dos disparos más, y los animales entendieron que el revólver de don Arcadio estaba hablando con ellos. Sin embargo, el más terco le dio una mordida más a un pie que tragó de un solo bocado. Pero fue lo último que hizo. Una bala le atravesó la cabeza. “Al principio no vi bien qué era lo que se estaban comiendo los perros -les dijo don Arcadio a los policías-, pero vi la cabecita del niño y entendí de golpe. Y ese perro se comió una patita... Por eso lo maté, para que le saquen de la panza las pruebas. Los otros dos se perdieron y no les disparé, porque podía matar una de mis vacas”. PUEDE LEER: Selección de Grandes Crímenes: El testigo que habló de más No era muy profunda, la abrieron con prisa y con mayor prisa la cerraron; luego pusieron algunas piedras sobre el montoncito de tierra húmeda y una rama recién arrancada. Adentro había sangre. Afuera quedaban los restos de un recién nacido. “Esto es de lo más horrible que he visto en años y años de carrera” -dijo el oficial de la Policía de investigación que llegó a la escena. “Por lo que queda de su entrepierna -agregó otro de los agentes-, era un varoncito. Los perros casi se lo comen todo”. “¿Quién pudo ser la desgraciada que hizo esto? -preguntó don Arcadio. “Debe ser de por aquí -respondió el oficial-. No creo que sea difícil encontrarla”. “Aquí hay muchas aldeas y caseríos, señor, y la gente se pierde en estas montañas”. “Don Arcadio -lo interrumpió uno de los hombres que estaban entre los curiosos, acompañados de mujeres y varios jóvenes-, entre cielo y tierra no hay nada oculto, y estoy seguro de que muy pronto nos vamos a dar cuenta de quién es la mal nacida que vino aquí a botar a su hijito”. “Debe ser de por aquí -dijo don Arcadio-. Y ha de ser una muchacha...” “O una esposa que le haya pagado mal al marido, don Arcadio; recuerde que muchos hombres de aquí se fueron de mojados, y no han regresado en años... Y... no es bueno que la mujer esté sola”. Entre los agentes de la Policía de Investigación había dos mujeres, que no solo estaban indignadas, estaban enfurecidas. “Vamos a encontrar a esa basura humana” -dijo una de ellas. “Aunque sea lo último que hagamos” -respondió la otra. Y la cacería comenzó aquella misma hora. Empezaron por hablar con los más viejos. Pero nadie sabía de alguna mujer que hubiera dado a luz en aquellos días. “Hay varias embarazadas -dijo una de las mujeres más ancianas-; pueden ir de aldea en aldea y allí las van a ver, pero de una que haya parido ayer, o en la madrugada, no sabemos nada. Tal vez me hubieran llamado porque yo soy partera profesionista, con permiso del ministerio de Salud... Y las conozco a casi todas”. “Vamos a regresar al pueblo -dijo el oficial-, los técnicos de Medicina Forense se van a llevar lo que queda del feto a Tegucigalpa... Nosotros vamos a informar a Juticalpa”. Acababa de decir esto cuando el chofer de una de las patrullas se acercó al oficial. “Mi inspector -le dijo-, lo están llamando por radio... Dicen que no le caen las llamadas a su teléfono”. “Mi inspector -dijo una voz chillante a través del aparato-, mire que aquí estamos en el centro de salud de Manto y tenemos una muchacha que se está vaciando en sangre... Y dice que ella mató a su hijito, pero lo demás no se le entiende... Según la enfermera, esta mujer tiene unas cinco horas de haber parido...” El oficial dio la orden, subieron a las patrullas y llegaron a Manto en un suspiro. No estaban lejos. Cuando llegaron al Centro de Salud corrieron hacia donde estaba la muchacha. Tenía los ojos abiertos y fijos, la boca abierta y seca, y estaba empapada en sangre. “Murió hace un par de minutos, señor -le dijo la enfermera al policía-; se desangró...” “Me dijeron que confesó que ella misma había matado a su hijito -exclamó el oficial-. ¿Qué fue lo que dijo?” La enfermera hizo una pausa. “Ella se llamaba Filomena; allí afuera están su abuela y su mamá. Tenía solo diecisiete años... Dicen que nunca se fijaron que la muchacha estuviera embarazada, creyeron que es que se había engordado porque trabajaba en la iglesia y allí el padre come bien...” “¿Trabajaba en la iglesia?”“Sí”.“¿De qué?” “Pues aquí nos conocemos todos, señor. Ella limpiaba, barría, le ayudaba al padre a llevar la casa...” “Bien... Bien... Dígame ¿qué fue lo que dijo sobre el niño muerto?” “Dijo que ella lo había matado. No es que se lo dijera a alguien en particular; lo decía como si estuviera delirando. Yo lo maté, decía, yo maté a mi hijito. Él me llevó al potrero y allí lo eché en un hoyo que hizo él mismo. Decía que no debía nacer aquel niño porque era hijo del pecado y estaba trayendo al diablo al mundo... Y que ella lo mató... Lo echó en el hoyo y estaba llorando...” “¿Eso decía?” TAMBIÉN: Selección de Grandes Crímenes: El día de la boda (Primera parte) “Sí -respondió la enfermera, limpiándose las lágrimas-. Yo le pregunté quién era él, pero me dijo...” “Llame al padrecito... Llame al padrecito. No dijo nada más, y murió”. “¿En qué puedo ayudarle a la Policía, señores? -dijo el padre, con voz suave y mirada serena y agradable- Soy el padre Santos”. “Padre -contestó el inspector-, ¿conoce usted a Filomena Zelaya?” “Sí, hijo, la conozco bien -se apresuró a responder el sacerdote, con las manos unidas-. ¿Qué es lo que pasa con ella? Por cierto, hoy tenía que venir temprano a la casa cural, y, a esta hora, no se ha presentado”. “Padre -dijo el inspector, levantando la voz-, sabemos que usted sedujo y embarazó a la muchacha... Y que fue con usted al potrero donde parió al muchachito y lo enterraron... Tenemos la confesión de la muchacha, que está en el Centro de Salud, casi desangrada”. “Esas son palabras del demonio, señor -respondió el sacerdote, sin que ni siquiera un solo músculo de su cara se moviera-, y no sé de qué es lo que me está hablando”. Hizo una pausa. “Dice que está en el centro de salud, ¿verdad? Pues vamos allá para verla”. El inspector se estremeció ante la serenidad del sacerdote. Había lanzado aquella acusación, seguro de que el hombre caería en la trampa, pero no había sangre en sus venas; era hielo, puro hielo. “¿Vamos?” -dijo. “¿Dónde anduvo usted esta mañana, padre?” -preguntó de repente el detective. “Haciendo mi trabajo pastoral, hijo -contestó el sacerdote-; ¿por qué lo pregunta?” Vio que los ojos del inspector estaban fijos en sus zapatos. “¡Ah! -exclamó-. El lodo en mis zapatos. Es normal en este pueblo, hijo. Mire, con las lluvias las calles están llenas de agua y de lodo. Y mi trabajo es pastorear ovejas, y voy de casa en casa muchas veces”. “¿Dónde estuvo hoy?” “En dos casas, hijo, muy temprano. Una, la casa de don Nicanor, que está muy anciano y lo está consumiendo el cáncer de próstata. Me llamaron para que fuera a darle los santos óleos... Y la segunda, la casa de doña Martha, que ya días no viene a misa, y, como bien sabe, me preocupo por eso... Vamos al centro de salud”.NOTA FINAL. Dos semanas después de entierro de Filomena, los moldes de las huellas de zapatos que los técnicos de inspecciones oculares levantaron en un molde de yeso en la escena del crimen estaban en manos del inspector. Con ellas, corrió hacia el pueblo. La iglesia estaba cerrada. “No podés catear una iglesia -le dijo uno de los jefes desde Tegucigalpa-; ni siquiera te podés meter a la casa cural... Preguntále al fiscal si tiene las agallas de pedirle eso a un juez... De por sí, el nombre de la Policía anda por el suelo, y vos metiéndote en una iglesia”. “Tengo el molde en yeso de las huellas que encontramos cerca de la fosa del niño -replicó el oficial-, creo que coincide con las de los zapatos del sacerdote. Yo se los vi puestos el día que encontraron al niño... Ya confirmamos las huellas de los zapatos de Filomena, la muchacha muerta. Ella dijo que el hombre fue con ella”. “Por muy seguro que estés, hablá con el fiscal, si el juez le da la orden”. En aquel momento se detuvo un pick up blanco frente a la iglesia; de él bajó el sacerdote. “¿Usted de nuevo por aquí, inspector? -le dijo el sacerdote-. Bienvenido. Imagino que desea hablar conmigo”. “Quiero ver sus zapatos”.“Aquí están”.“Los que andaba puestos hace dos semanas, cuando murió Filomena...” “¿Los que usted me vio llenos de barro?” NO TE PUEDES PERDER: Selección de Grandes Crímenes: El día de la boda “Esos”. “Pues ya no los tengo. Los deseché. Estaban gastados y viejos”. “Gastados del tacón hacia afuera -exclamó el inspector-, y el izquierdo, con el centro de la plantilla más gastado que el derecho”. “¡Ah!, no soy tan observador... Estaban viejos; los tiré a la basura, y como tengo por costumbre quemarlo todo”. “Usted llevó a la muerte a Filomena”. “¡Ah!” “Y la obligó a matar a su hijo...” El sacerdote, un hombre de unos treinta y dos años, alto, delgado, bien parecido y de carácter apacible, exclamó de nuevo: “¡Ah!” “Voy a acusarlo directamente... Usted es el asesino”. El sacerdote sonrió. “Usted me agrada -le dijo al oficial-; hombres como usted, tan apasionados, son los que hacen que sea verdad eso que dicen de la Policía: que es más lo que inventa que lo que descubre”. ¿Cuál era la verdad? ¿Tenía razón el oficial? Cinco meses después recibió una llamada. Era una mujer. “El padre Santos es un maldito -decía la voz enfurecida-; él embarazó a Filomena y la obligó a deshacerse del niño. A mí me preñó y me exigió que abortara... Y yo le hice caso, porque tengo un novio en san Esteban... Pero, tuve que ir a Tegucigalpa para que me hicieran un legrado... Y a él no le importó... Mi novio me dejó y el padre Santos ni siquiera ha venido a verme”. “¿Quién habla?” -preguntó el inspector. “Usted me conoció cuando trajeron a Filomena desangrándose...” “¡La enfermera!” La comunicación se cortó. Cuando el inspector regresó al pueblo, el padre ya no estaba. Lo trasladaron a un pueblo en las montañas de Guatemala. La enfermera, joven y bonita, se recuperaba en una cama, entre las sombras de su cuarto y la ira de su madre. “Fue el padre -le dijo al oficial-, y no solo lo hizo con Filomena y conmigo... Le voy a dar la lista”.
data.translatedTitle: Selection of Great Crimes: Father Santos' List (Part One)
data.translatedDescription: DOGS. The road was wet. It was a royal road, lined with trees that stood behind a long old stone wall. Beyond them grew the green cornfields, full of life, with beautiful corn with long golden hair. On the other side, cattle grazed in a pasture that stretched away until it was lost in the forest that began at the foot of the mountains. It was early, the sun was peeking out in the distance and rising slowly under a gray sky that was beginning to fill with rain. Nothing is more beautiful than the countryside, but when it seems like a paradise and not the scene of a crime as horrible as it is detestable. Behind a huge rock, surrounded by bushes, were three large, angry dogs that were snarling, barking and showing each other their long fangs, stained with fresh blood. They ate and fought over the food they had just dug up from a kind of makeshift grave that someone had dug between the rock and the wall, where the earth was softer and covered by the dense branches of the bushes. They tore, chewed, swallowed, and bit at each other. One ate a little arm, crushing the bones with hunger; The second tore off what was left of a small leg and the tiny foot, while the third got stuck with the entrails that were still attached to a long umbilical cord. On one side was a little head full of blood and dirt, already separated from the small trunk, which would soon disappear between the voracious snouts of the dogs. How had they found that sinister feast? Well, no one could say. It was evident that they dug with desperation, the kind that causes hunger, and together they pulled out of that grave the remains that they swallowed in great strides. Of course, this was a pasture, not a cemetery, and what the dogs ate was what was left of a fetus, perhaps a newborn child that someone did not want to come into the world. Don Arcadio got off his horse. From that height you could see what was happening near the rock on the wall. He took out his revolver from his waist and fired two shots into the air. The dogs, more hungry than scared, saw him dripping blood from between his teeth and one of them dared to growl, defiant. Two more shots, and the animals understood that Don Arcadio's revolver was talking to them. However, the most stubborn one took one more bite of a foot that he swallowed in one bite. But it was the last thing he did. A bullet went through his head. "At first I didn't really see what the dogs were eating," Don Arcadio told the police, "but I saw the little boy's head and I suddenly understood. And that dog ate a paw... That's why I killed him, so they could take the evidence out of his belly. The other two got lost and I didn't shoot them, because I could kill one of my cows." YOU CAN READ: Selection of Great Crimes: The witness who spoke too much It was not very deep, they opened it in haste and with greater haste they closed it; Then they put some stones on the little pile of damp earth and a freshly torn branch. There was blood inside. Outside were the remains of a newborn. “This is the most horrible thing I have seen in years and years of my career,” said the investigating police officer who arrived at the scene. "From what's left of his crotch," added another of the agents, "it was a little boy. The dogs almost ate everything." "Who could be the unfortunate woman who did this?" asked Don Arcadio. "She must be from around here," the officer responded. I don't think it will be difficult to find her." "There are many villages and hamlets here, sir, and people get lost in these mountains." "Don Arcadio," interrupted one of the men who were among the curious, accompanied by women and several young people, "between heaven and earth there is nothing hidden, and I am sure that very soon we will realize who the ill-born woman is who came here to throw away her little son." "She must be from around here," said Don Arcadio. " And it has to be a girl…” “Or a wife who has paid her husband poorly, Don Arcadio; remember that many men here left because they were wet, and haven't returned in years... And... it's not good for the woman to be alone." Among the Investigative Police agents there were two women, who were not only indignant, they were enraged. "We're going to find that human trash," said one of them. "Even if it's the last thing we do," answered the other. And the hunt began that same hour. They began by talking to the oldest ones. But no one knew of any woman who had given birth. in those days. “There are several pregnant women,” said one of the older women; They can go from village to village and they will see them there, but we don't know anything about one that gave birth yesterday, or in the morning. Maybe they would have called me because I am a professional midwife, with permission from the Ministry of Health... And I know almost all of them." "We are going to return to the town," said the officer, "the Forensic Medicine technicians are going to take what remains of the fetus to Tegucigalpa... We are going to inform Juticalpa." He had just said this when the driver of one of the patrol cars approached the officer. "My inspector," he told him, "they are calling you on the radio... They say that they don't receive calls to your phone." "My inspector," said a shrill voice through the device, "look here we are in the Manto health center and we have a girl who is emptying herself of blood... And she says that she killed her little son, but the rest is not understood... According to the nurse, this woman has been giving birth for about five hours..." The officer gave the order, they got into the patrol cars and arrived at Manto in a flash. They were not far away. When they arrived at the Health Center they ran towards where the girl. Her eyes were open and fixed, her mouth was open and dry, and she was soaked in blood. “She died a couple of minutes ago, sir,” the nurse told the police officer. "She bled..." "They told me that she confessed that she herself had killed her little son," the officer exclaimed. “What did he say?” The nurse paused. “She was called Filomena; His grandmother and his mother are out there. She was only seventeen years old... They say they never noticed that the girl was pregnant, they thought she had gotten fat because she worked in the church and there the father eats well...” “Did she work in the church?” “Yes.” “Of what?” “Well, we all know each other here, sir. She cleaned, she swept, she helped her father run the house…” “Good… Good… Tell me what did you say about the dead child?” “He said she had killed him. Not that I said it to anyone in particular; He said it like he was delirious. I killed him, he said, I killed my little son. He took me to the pasture and there I threw him into a hole he made himself. She said that that child should not be born because he was a child of sin and was bringing the devil into the world... And that she killed him... She threw him into the hole and he was crying..." "Is that what she said?" ALSO: Selection of Great Crimes: The Wedding Day (Part One) “Yes,” the nurse answered, wiping away her tears. I asked him who he was, but he told me..." "Call the little father... Call the little father. He didn't say anything else, and he died." "How can I help the Police, gentlemen? -said the father, with a soft voice and a serene and pleasant look- “I am Father Santos.” “Father,” the inspector answered, “do you know Filomena Zelaya?” “Yes, son, I know her well,” the priest responded quickly, with his hands joined. What's wrong with her? By the way, today he had to come early to the priest's house, and at this time, he has not shown up." "Father," said the inspector, raising his voice, "we know that you seduced and impregnated the girl... And that she went with you to the pasture where she gave birth to the little boy and they buried him... We have the confession of the girl, who is in the Health Center, almost bleeding to death." "Those are the words of the devil, sir," the priest responded, without even a single word. Only the muscle of his face moved - and I don't know what he's talking about." He paused. "He says he's at the health center, right? Well, let's go there to see her." The inspector shuddered at the serenity of the priest. He had launched that accusation, sure that the man would fall into the trap, but there was no blood in his veins; it was ice, pure ice. "Shall we?" -he said. “Where were you this morning, father?” -the detective suddenly asked. “Doing my pastoral work, son,” answered the priest; “Why do you ask?” He saw that the inspector's eyes were fixed on his shoes. “Ah! -he exclaimed-. The mud on my shoes. It's normal in this town, son. Look, with the rains the streets are full of water and mud. And my job is to herd sheep, and I go from house to house many times.” “Where were you today?” “In two houses, son, very early. One, the house of Don Nicanor, who is very old and is being consumed by prostate cancer. They called me to go give her the holy oils... And the second, Doña Martha's house, who has not been coming to mass for days, and, as you well know, I worry about that... Let's go to the health center." FINAL NOTE. Two weeks after Filomena's burial, the molds of the shoe prints that the eye inspection technicians raised in a plaster mold at the crime scene were in the hands of the inspector. With them, he ran towards the town. The church was closed. “You can't search a church,” one of the leaders told him from Tegucigalpa; You can't even get into the priest's house... Ask the prosecutor if he has the guts to ask that of a judge... In itself, the name of the Police is on the ground, and you are getting into a church." "I have the plaster cast of the footprints that we found near the child's grave," the officer replied, "I think it matches those of the priest's shoes. I saw them wearing them the day they found the child... We have already confirmed the shoe prints of Filomena, the dead girl. She said that the man went with her." "No matter how sure you are, talk to the prosecutor, if the judge gives him the order." At that moment a white pickup truck stopped in front of the church; the priest got out of it. "Are you here again, inspector? -the priest told him-. Welcome. I imagine you want to talk to me.” “I want to see your shoes.” “Here they are.” “The ones you were wearing two weeks ago, when Filomena died…” “The ones you saw covered in mud?” YOU CAN'T MISS: Selection of Great Crimes: The wedding day “Those”. “Well, I don't have them anymore. I threw them away. They were worn out and old." "Worn out from the heel outwards," exclaimed the inspector, "and the left one, with the center of the insole more worn out than the right one." "Ah!, I'm not that observant... They were old; I threw them in the trash, and as I have the habit of burning everything.” “You led Filomena to death.” “Ah!” “And he forced her to kill her son…” The priest, a man of about thirty-two years old, tall, thin, good-looking and of a mild disposition, exclaimed again: “Ah!” “I am going to accuse you directly... You are the murderer.” The priest smiled. “I like you,” he told the officer; Men like you, so passionate, are the ones who make what they say about the Police true: that what they invent is more than what they discover." What was the truth? Was the officer right? Five months later he received a call. It was a woman. "Father Santos is a bastard," said the angry voice; He impregnated Filomena and forced her to get rid of the child. He got me pregnant and demanded that I abort... And I listened to him, because I have a boyfriend in San Esteban... But, I had to go to Tegucigalpa to have a curettage done... And he didn't care... My boyfriend left me and Father Santos hasn't even come to see me.” “Who's talking?” -asked the inspector. “You met me when they brought in Filomena bleeding to death…” “The nurse!” Communication was cut off. When the inspector returned to the town, the father was no longer there. They moved him to a town in the mountains of Guatemala. The nurse, young and pretty, was recovering in a bed, between the shadows of her room and the anger of her mother. “It was the father,” he told the officer, “and he not only did it with Filomena and me... I'm going to give you the list.”

data.title: Stanje na putevima u BiH: Na nekoliko graničnih prijelaza zabilježene duge kolone vozila
data.description: Na putevima u Bosni i Hercegovini jutros se saobraća bez vanrednih ograničenja, uz izuzetak dionica na kojima se izvode sanacioni radovi. Početak je radne sedmice, pa se tokom dana očekuje pojačana frekvencija saobraćaja na prilazima većim gradskim centrima, a zbog sezone godišnjih odmora i na graničnim prelazima prema Hrvatskoj i Crnoj Gori.
data.translatedTitle: Road conditions in Bosnia and Herzegovina: Long lines of vehicles were recorded at several border crossings
data.translatedDescription: Roads in Bosnia and Herzegovina are open to traffic this morning without extraordinary restrictions, with the exception of sections where rehabilitation works are being carried out. It is the beginning of the working week, so increased traffic frequency is expected during the day on the approaches to larger city centers, and due to the holiday season, also at the border crossings to Croatia and Montenegro.

data.title: Huti iz Jemena objavili snimak lansiranja raketa i dronova na saudijske položaje: "Oficiri su devastirani"

data.translatedTitle: The Houthis from Yemen published a video of rockets and drones being launched at Saudi positions: "Officers are devastated"
data.translatedDescription: Yemen's Houthis released footage showing the launch of ballistic missiles and drones targeting Saudi military concentrations and weapons depots in Mokha.

data.title: Meloni dobila ozbiljnu konkurenciju: Bivši general šarmira radikalnu desnicu i postaje sve veća prijetnja premijerki
data.description: Premijerka Italije Giorgia Meloni je već nekoliko godina daleko najpopularnija političarka koja pripada desnici u Italiji, ali bi se to moglo promijeniti. Na njeno mjesto želi doći Roberto Vannacci, a posljednje ankete pokazuju da je sve popularniji.
data.translatedTitle: Meloni received serious competition: The former general charms the radical right and becomes an increasing threat to the Prime Minister
data.translatedDescription: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has been by far the most popular right-wing politician in Italy for several years, but that could change. Roberto Vannacci wants to take her place, and the latest polls show that he is increasingly popular.

data.title: Jasna poruka Irana: Bez ustupaka SAD-a neće doći do otvaranja Hormuškog moreuza
data.description: Iran je saopćio da je blizu postizanja konačnog sporazuma s Omanom kojim bi se definisali novi plovni putevi između dvije zemlje kroz Hormuški moreuz, ali su iz Teherana ponovili da Sjedinjene Američke Države moraju ispuniti i druge uslove, piše Reuters.
data.translatedTitle: A clear message from Iran: Without US concessions, the opening of the Strait of Hormuz will not happen
data.translatedDescription: Iran said it was close to reaching a final agreement with Oman that would define new waterways between the two countries through the Strait of Hormuz, but Tehran reiterated that the United States must meet other conditions, writes Reuters.

data.title: Dronovi su za Evropu sve veća prijetnja, a upozorenje stiže iz Londona i Njemačke: "Stanje je alarmantno"
data.description: Sveobuhvatna analiza incidenata s dronovima u Evropi posljednjih godina, a koju je sproveo londonski Međunarodni institut za strateške studije (IISS) otkriva značajne ranjivosti u načinu na koji države reaguju na ovu vrstu prijetnje.
data.translatedTitle: Drones are a growing threat to Europe, and a warning comes from London and Germany: "The situation is alarming"
data.translatedDescription: A comprehensive analysis of drone incidents in Europe in recent years by the London-based International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) reveals significant vulnerabilities in the way states respond to this type of threat.

data.title: Lukavac rješava višegodišnji problem vodosnabdijevanja, filter stanica Modrac prelazi u vlasništvo grada
data.description: Nakon višegodišnjih problema vodosnabdijevanja, Lukavac ulazi u važnu fazu rješavanja pitanja od kojeg zavisi stabilnost gradskog vodovodnog sistema. Naime, za filter stanicu Modrac i vodne objekte osigurano je 5,3 miliona konvertibilnih maraka, a neophodan ugovor je potpisan.
data.translatedTitle: Lukavac solves the perennial problem of water supply, the Modrac filter station becomes the property of the city
data.translatedDescription: After several years of water supply problems, Lukavac is entering an important phase of solving the issue on which the stability of the city's water supply system depends. Namely, 5.3 million convertible marks were secured for the filter station Modrac and water facilities, and the necessary contract was signed.

data.translatedDescription: Research shows that breakups most often occur in three crisis moments: during the first year due to the loss of initial chemistry, between the third and fifth year due to mismatched goals, and around the seventh year due to the accumulated emotional distancing of the partner.

data.title: Duty and a Creative Bartender: How a Civilian Woman Joined Azov
data.description: Margarita "Margo" Koldanova once managed marketing for Kyiv coffee shops and restaurants. Feeling that volunteering wasn't enough, she began asking how a civilian could serve – then discovered a former bartender she knew had joined Azov. Their conversations became a relationship, and eventually a marriage. Margo now works in Azov's media team, balancing a modest salary, freelance work, and the strange rhythm of loving someone inside the same war she's fighting.

data.title: Russia Escalates Drone Strikes on Ukraine’s Naftogaz
data.description: Russian forces have significantly increased drone strikes against Naftogaz Group infrastructure, targeting Ukrnafta production assets and a drilling rig on Aug. 9. The attacks caused substantial damage, halting operations at the affected sites, though no casualties were reported. These strikes follow a series of attacks on Aug. 7 and 8 that damaged seven Ukrnafta filling stations across three regions and injured one employee. Acting Naftogaz CEO Sergii Fedorenko stated the strikes are a deliberate attempt to cripple Ukraine’s energy sector ahead of the winter heating season.

data.title: US Weapons Shortage Sparks Global Security Fears – NYT
data.description: The ongoing US war with Iran has severely depleted American military stockpiles, particularly expensive Patriot interceptors, ATACMS, and Tomahawk missiles. The shortage has forced Washington to delay arms shipments to European and Asian partners while stripping the Indo-Pacific region of critical air defense and naval assets. The deficit is acutely affecting Ukraine’s ability to counter Russian missile attacks. In response, Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg and the Pentagon have urgently demanded that defense contractors accelerate production timelines within 21 days to replenish the depleted arsenals.

data.title: WHO Chief Says Warehouse Hit in Ukraine
data.description: A World Health Organization humanitarian warehouse in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro was destroyed by a strike on Friday, Aug 7. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus confirmed the destruction, noting that staff and drivers narrowly escaped the attack after evacuating 130 pallets of emergency medical supplies intended for frontline facilities. No casualties were reported. The WHO has recorded over 3,148 attacks on Ukrainian healthcare since the 2022 invasion, resulting in 240 deaths. The incident follows recent condemnations from Doctors Without Borders, which accused Russia of a deliberate strategy to dismantle Ukraine’s healthcare system.

data.title: Russia Hit Odesa with 11 Missiles and 100 Drones in a Massive Attack
data.description: A massive Russian attack on Aug. 9 targeted the Odesa region with 11 missiles and up to 100 UAVs, including “Banderol” loitering munitions. The strike injured 12 people, damaged residential buildings and energy infrastructure, and caused power and water outages across parts of the city. The assault is part of a week-long Russian bombardment involving over 60 missiles and 3,100 drones and guided bombs, which also included a double-tap strike on a high-rise in Kharkiv’s Saltivka district that killed three people and injured at least 37.

data.title: Combat Drone Explodes Near Moldova-Ukraine Border
data.description: An explosion and subsequent fire occurred near the Moldovan village of Crocmaz in the Ștefan Vodă district at approximately 1:20 p.m. local time on Sunday. Preliminary information from Moldovan police indicates the blast was caused by fragments of a combat drone. No casualties were reported, and a specialized explosives team is conducting a forensic examination of the site. The incident adds to a growing list of drone crashes within Moldovan territory, following the discovery of Russian Geran-2 wreckage near Văleni on Aug. 5 and an explosive-laden drone near Tudora in March.

data.title: Iran Issues Demands to US for Reopening Strait of Hormuz
data.description: Tehran has issued a list of demands to the US in exchange for reopening the strategic Strait of Hormuz. Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohammad Bagher Zolqadr demanded the lifting of the US naval blockade, troop withdrawals, a complete cessation of hostilities, compensation for damages, and access to frozen assets. The White House has not yet commented. The demands follow President Donald Trump’s Aug. 2 decision to suspend a planned US air campaign against Iran to allow for negotiations aimed at securing the immediate reopening of the strait.

data.title: Russian Strike on Zhytomyr Injures 3 Civilians
data.description: A Russian attack on the Zhytomyr region on Aug. 9 injured three civilians and caused fires at civilian infrastructure and private property. The weekend assaults resulted in casualties across the country, including a direct hit on a high-rise in Kharkiv that left three dead and 37 injured, ballistic strikes on Odesa that damaged port and energy infrastructure, and bombardments in Pavlohrad and Izium that wounded multiple civilians, including young children.

data.title: Russia Fires 61 Missiles, 1,560 Drones, 1,540 Bombs at Ukraine in a Week
data.description: Following a weekend of Russian strikes, President Volodymyr Zelensky reported that Moscow launched 61 missiles, over 1,560 attack drones, and 1,540 guided aerial bombs against Ukraine in the past week. Bombardments on Sunday caused casualties and infrastructure damage. In Kharkiv, a direct hit on a multi-story building left three dead and 37 injured. In Odesa, nighttime ballistic and drone strikes injured at least eight people and damaged port facilities. Meanwhile, Saturday strikes on Pavlohrad and Izium left numerous civilians wounded, including several children. Zelensky reiterated his call for increased Western pressure, sanctions, and air defense support.

data.title: Putin Plans Covert Mobilization, North Korean Deployments
data.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that Russian President Vladimir Putin is preparing a massive, unannounced mobilization through “shadow contracts” and border closures in a desperate bid to secure a victory in the Donbas. Zelensky stated that Putin will likely attempt to “twist the Anchorage terms”—referring to previous backchannel discussions with the US – to present a win to the Russian public. Furthermore, Zelensky revealed that Russia plans to deploy up to 50,000 North Korean troops to its territory for combat training.

Zelensky stated that Putin will likely attempt to “twist the Anchorage terms”—referring to previous backchannel discussions with the US – to present a win to the Russian public. Furthermore, Zelensky revealed that Russia plans to deploy up to 50,000 North Korean troops to its territory for combat training.

data.title: Belarus Opposition Waits for Its Solidarity Moment
data.description: Almost six years after Alexander Lukashenko claimed a fraudulent election victory, Belarusian opposition leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya compares her exiled democratic movement to Poland’s underground Solidarity. While Belarus experienced a similar mass mobilization in 2020, Lukashenko’s immediate and brutal crackdown prevented the movement from establishing roots inside the country. Operating as a proto-government in exile, the opposition faces internal divisions following recent prisoner releases. Unlike Poland in 1989, the Belarusian regime remains financially and politically supported by Russia.

data.title: Ukraine Strikes Russian S-400 Missile System, Radars, Shadow Fleet Vessels
data.description: Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces (USF) Commander Robert “Magyar” Brovdi announced that drone operators struck multiple high-value Russian targets overnight on Aug. 8. The strikes hit an S-400 “Triumph” anti-aircraft missile system in Gelendzhik, a Tor system, a Pantsir-S1 system, two radar stations, and three “shadow fleet” vessels in the Black Sea. The attacks are part of the broader “Operation MoLoChKa,” which has targeted over 200 Russian vessels since early July, effectively blocking the Kerch Strait.

data.title: Bulgaria Identifies Ukrainian Decoy Drone Found Near Gas Pipeline
data.description: The Bulgarian Defense Ministry announced that the drone which crashed and exploded near the Kardam border crossing on Aug. 8 was likely a Ukrainian “Maiia” decoy drone, adding that there is no evidence the crash was intentional. In response to the incident, the Bulgarian Foreign Ministry has summoned Ukrainian Ambassador Olesya Ilashchuk for an explanation on Monday, Aug. 10. Ukrainian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi stressed that Ukraine did not intentionally target Bulgaria and is fully cooperating with the investigation. He emphasized that the root cause of such regional security incidents remains Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine. The drone had entered Bulgarian airspace from Romania, flying low enough to evade air defense systems, and detonated in a field about one kilometer from a Trans-Balkan gas pipeline compressor station.

data.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky said that the first combat deployment of a domestically produced Ukrainian ballistic missile could happen this fall. data.title: The sealed watermelon of the Mecca Agreement
data.description: TEHRAN — Three leaders signed a promise inside Al-Safa Palace on Friday: an armed attack on Saudi Arabia, Turkey or Pakistan will be treated as an attack on all three. Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan compared the clause to NATO’s Article 5. The full text stays sealed, unread outside the rooms where it was drafted. data.description: António Aly Silva » aaly.silva@gmail.com » aaly_silva@hotmail.com » Tel. (+245) 668 31 13
data.translatedTitle: Cabral gave up all the comfort he had at the time (in Lisbon and Bissau), and decided to give his life to his people. data.title: DSP o Maquiavélico Ganancioso
data.description: Guineenses, mais uma vez, venho para vos alertar sobre o perigo que Domingos Simões Pereira representa para a Guiné-Bissau. Faço esse alerta a todos os guineenses sem exceção que se encontre no país ou no estrangeiro, ao PAIGC em especial e na pessoa do Cipriano Cassamá em concreto. Alerta esse sobre o verdadeiro DSP, o verdadeiro espírito que move esse sujeito, o qual alguns ainda continuam a acreditar para não dizer adorar. Domingos Simões Pereira é um manipulador, um verdadeiro chantagista e calculista provavelmente, tipo de comportamento que ultrapassa o nível de psicopata. U m ambicioso desmedido, um verdadeiro criminoso que sabe como e quando cometer o crime. Ele jamais coabitaria não só com JOMAV, assim como com qualquer presidente que seria eleito, a não ser o que ele apoiou disfarçadamente. Isto porque ele tem sua própria agenda, e o PAIGC é simplesmente uma plataforma para sua concretização. DSP jamais coabitaria com JOMAV porque o seu candidato preferido era o Paulo Gomes e sempre será, o qual juntamente com Tchitchi vão delineando mecanismo de modo a serem os novos donos da Guiné-Bissau. Segundo eles este é um processo a médio prazo, e é preciso coragem e paciência para concretiza-lo. Ganhar o congresso não importa em que circunstância e ter novamente o partido na mão, é uma fase concluída em proveito deles, enquanto verdadeiros militantes do PAIGC estão a bater palmas. Depois dessa eleição legislativa, não importa o resultado, o Cipriano Cassama que se prepare a mala ou fica de bico fechado, pois o candidato preferido para o partido será o Paulo Gomes, e esse sim deve ter a voz dentro do partido. DSP é um ambicioso desmedido, nunca teve consideração por ninguém, JOMAV muito menos, o sujeito é um maquiavélico nato, Cipriano Casama será descartado quando menos esperar podes tomar a nota. Guineenses, falar do Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi é falar do MCCI e demais outras organizações e personalidades camufladas no nosso país. Esses dois indivíduos são os principais financiadores do MCCI e demais outras personalidades boca de aluguel na cidade de Bissau. O MCCI, Milícia idealizado por JBV e DSP, agora financiado e dirigido por "futuro triângulo do poder" ou seja, "DSP, Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi", têm 3 principais objectivos: 1º Perturbar a ordem pública em nome da cidadania, difamar e tentar descredibilizar qualquer que seja organizações ou indivíduos não alinhados ao triângulo, de modo a suportar suas caminhadas na busca do poder. 2º Caso se concretize o objectivo do triângulo, o papel da Milícia do MCCI passará a ser de vigilância constante a todos os adversários de modo a garantir falsa paz social e o poder de controlo. 3º Tentar ganhar credibilidade junto das organizações internacionais e regionais, através de suas visitas e actividades de fachada, para quando houver as tais actividades de perturbações de ordem pública, poderem ganhar notoriedade. Mas isso não deve preocupar ninguém, pois estão bem identificados e bem caçados, dentro e fora da Guiné-Bissau. Não tenho nada contra ninguém, mas quem continuar a perturbar verdadeira paz social dos guineenses em troca de benefícios como sempre foi nos últimos anos dessa crise, e que sempre tenho tolerado, então que fique claro "estou firme e determinado para tudo e todos". Para finalizar, gostaria de vos deixar uma reflexão com a seguinte frase: " Domingos Simões Pereira é um perigo grave para o futuro do país ". Chega, chega não podemos continuar a viver nessa turbulência vida toda, meus irmãos guineenses, não é saudável, é tóxico, não é justo para um povo que tanto sofreu. data.title: DSP, UM PERIGO GRAVE PARA FUTURO DO PAÍS
data.description: Os meios de comunicação também são as formas de manipulação mais utilizadas pelos poderes políticos, dado o seu impacto social. As informações são manipuladas não apenas tendo em vista omitir factos relevantes, mas também distorcer o conteúdo da informação veiculada, produzir ou forjar a opinião pública, de modo que a mesma se ajuste às ideias dos gananciosos. A única forma dos cidadãos evitarem cair nestes processos de manipulação é tornarem-se mais vigilantes em relação às instituições democráticas e aos órgãos de informação, adoptando uma atitude de permanente reflexão crítica sobre a informação que lhes é fornecida. Na Guiné-Bissau, nos últimos anos, cresceu exponencialmente o número de pessoas mediocres, pessoas sem escrúpulos ligadas à produção de rádios e outros meios de comunicação com influencia na nossa sociedade, gente que apesar da sua enorme influência na sociedade, trabalha na mais completa impunidade e sem qualquer controlo ético/democrático. Obcecado pelo poder, ciente da dificuldade do povo guineense em avaliar informações, ciente do poder dos instrumentos de comunicação, Domingos Simões Pereira (DSP) nunca menosprezou esses instrumentos para atingir seu objectivo, sempre usou-os de forma desonesta como agora está a fazer tudo por tudo para manter no controlo desses veicúlos, mesmo que isso custe a vida dos outros. Governou na corrupção, no nepotismo e no desvios de somas astronómicas do dinheiro de povo, que muito serviria para investimentos na saúde, educação e outros serviços publicos, para beneficiar familiares e amigos. Finge que preocupa com os problemas do país, mas só engana o povo honesto, humilde e trabalhador que infelizmente sofre muito, não sei até quando, devido a sua paciência e tolerância aos governantes como DSP, criminoso travestido em politico que vive na custa de povo e acima de tudo ainda fa-lo refem do próprio suor. Roubou e decepcionou tanto não só aos guineenses assim como a comunidade internacional que sempre acreditou que o sujeito era ideal para ajudar esse povo a sair do ciclo de sofrimento que parece infinito. Foi demitido, não conformou e está a fazer tudo na medida do possível para continuar a complicar a vida dos guineenses. Razão disso é que depois de perder a batalha nos meios de comunicações mais modernos nomeadamente os blogues onde investiu grandes somas do dinheiro de povo, para fazer a lavagem cerebral dos menos instruídos e não só. Fugiu do facebook onde sempre frequentava e comunicava com todos tentado passar a mensagem de um politico moderno e aberto a diálogo/opiniões, mas que afinal era simplesmente um falso modernista. Caiu a mascara e já não consegue enganar ninguem, pois a sua credibilidade está abaixo de zero, para não dizer outra coisa. Camaradas, para conhecimento geral, com o dinheiro roubado que custou suor de povo guineense, DSP decidiu avançar com um outro novo plano maquiavelico, para criar a sua própria estação de rádio. data.translatedTitle: DSP, A SERIOUS DANGER TO THE FUTURE OF THE COUNTRY
data.translatedDescription: The media is also the form of manipulation most used by political powers, given its social impact. Information is manipulated not only with a view to omitting relevant facts, but also distorting the content of the information conveyed, producing or forging public opinion, so that it fits the ideas of the greedy. The only way for citizens to avoid falling into these manipulation processes is to become more vigilant in relation to democratic institutions and information bodies, adopting an attitude of permanent critical reflection on the information provided to them. In Guinea-Bissau, in recent years, the number of mediocre people has grown exponentially, unscrupulous people linked to the production of radio stations and other means of communication with influence in our society, people who, despite their enormous influence in society, work with complete impunity and without any ethical/democratic control. Obsessed with power, aware of the difficulty of the Guinean people in evaluating information, aware of the power of communication instruments, Domingos Simões Pereira (DSP) never underestimated these instruments to achieve his objective, he always used them dishonestly and is now doing everything he can to maintain control of these vehicles, even if it costs the lives of others. He ruled through corruption, nepotism and the embezzlement of astronomical sums of people's money, which would largely be used for investments in health, education and other public services, to benefit family and friends. He pretends to care about the country's problems, but he only deceives the honest, humble and hard-working people who unfortunately suffer a lot, I don't know for how long, due to his patience and tolerance towards rulers like DSP, a criminal disguised as a politician who lives at the expense of the people and, above all, still holds them hostage to his own sweat. He stole and disappointed so much not only the Guineans but also the international community that always believed that the guy was ideal to help these people get out of the cycle of suffering that seems infinite. He was fired, did not comply and is doing everything possible to continue complicating the lives of Guineans. The reason for this is that after losing the battle in the most modern means of communications, namely blogs, where he invested large sums of people's money, to brainwash the less educated and others. He fled Facebook where he always visited and communicated with everyone, trying to convey the message of a modern politician open to dialogue/opinions, but who, in the end, was simply a false modernist. The mask has fallen and it is no longer able to deceive anyone, as its credibility is below zero, to say the least. Comrades, for general knowledge, with the stolen money that cost the Guinean people sweat, DSP decided to move forward with another new Machiavellian plan, to create its own radio station. In a statement, the party held the Lebanese authorities responsible for the continuation of these attacks, citing their insistence on pursuing […]

data.title: Ramaphosa asks families to help identify 20,000 women who marched in 1956
data.description: PRETORIA – President Cyril Ramaphosa delivered his keynote address at the Union Buildings in Pretoria on National Women’s Day, Sunday 9 August, marking 70 years since the historic 1956 women’s march. He vowed to step up the fight against gender-based violence and economic inequality.
